16:I[12454,["/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/08cykig6vtx_p.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/07qi2okp-.yp9.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0frujd.eyhz4o.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0n4z.7yu76je-.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0otjhi71vbmnx.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/0j1uy9t~zxcf0.js","/paper-daily-site/_next/static/chunks/1304s0wcp2kce.js"],"WeeklyView"]
17:T893,FROST has two main ingredients: real-anchored utility estimation and conditional filtering.

For utility estimation, each training step draws both a real batch and a synthetic batch. The method maintains an exponential moving average of gradients from recent real batches, which serves as a smoothed reference direction for the real-data objective. Each synthetic sample is then scored by the alignment between its gradient and this real-gradient reference. The intuition is straightforward: if a synthetic sample pushes parameters in a direction similar to what recent real data prefers, it is more likely to be useful; if it points away, it is more likely to be harmful or off-distribution.

The second ingredient is conditional filtering. The authors argue that per-sample gradient utility is noisy, so filtering every batch aggressively can remove useful supervision. They first aggregate utilities at the batch level and compare the batch mean against recent history to determine whether the batch falls inside a moderate utility band. Batches inside the band are kept as-is. Only out-of-band batches trigger sample-level filtering, where interquartile-range thresholds are used to retain or discard examples within the batch. This design is meant to avoid overreacting to stochastic gradient noise while still rescuing good samples from otherwise weak batches.

Relative to common synthetic-data selection methods, FROST differs in three ways. It does not require a separate pretrained feature extractor for fidelity/diversity scoring, so it avoids expensive offline preprocessing of the full synthetic pool. It does not need a held-out validation set or an external judge, because the real training stream itself provides the anchor. And it is online: utility is recomputed as the model evolves, rather than assigned once in a static preprocessing stage.

From a pretraining perspective, the hidden assumption is that an EMA of real-data gradients is a stable proxy for the target objective. That seems plausible in moderate-scale fine-tuning, but it is less obvious in large mixed-corpus pretraining where gradient noise, domain conflict, and real/synthetic ratios can be very different.18:T621,The paper evaluates FROST on image classification, LLM fine-tuning for text-to-SQL, and a large industrial ads re-ranking system. On the public benchmarks, it filters out roughly 20% to 30% of synthetic data while outperforming training on the full synthetic pool.

The reported gains are 0.58% to 1.14% absolute accuracy improvement across three synthetic image generators, and 0.9% improvement on text-to-SQL fine-tuning. The industrial result is more telling in practical terms: using the full noisy synthetic pool causes a 0.211% relative NE regression compared with the real-only baseline, while FROST turns that into a 0.096% relative NE improvement. The authors note that gains around 0.02% are already considered meaningful in mature production recommenders, so the industrial effect size is not trivial.

Methodologically, the matched-drop-ratio comparison is important. The paper compares selection methods under the same synthetic-data discard rate, which makes the gains more attributable to better selection rather than simply using less data. Also worth checking is the ablation on batch-level gating plus sample-level filtering versus always-on per-sample filtering, since that is the part intended to control gradient-noise sensitivity.

The main caveat is scope. The LLM experiment is a downstream fine-tuning task, not large-scale language-model pretraining. The paper does not establish that real-anchored gradient utility remains stable or cost-effective for next-token pretraining with large synthetic corpora or reasoning-heavy synthetic mixtures.19:T4d9,For a skim read, start with the Introduction and Method to understand the logic of real-anchored utility and conditional filtering. Then read the text-to-SQL experiment and the main ablations. Around 20 to 30 minutes should be enough to decide whether the idea is portable to your own data pipeline.

Focus on four details. First, inspect how utility is computed in practice: full gradients, projected gradients, or some approximation. That determines scalability. Second, check how the real-gradient EMA is updated and stabilized, because the whole method depends on the anchor being reliable. Third, read the calibration rule for batch means and the IQR-based sample filtering, since that is where the paper tries to avoid over-filtering under noisy gradients. Fourth, look for behavior across different drop ratios, synthetic-data quality levels, and training stages.

If your interest is pretraining data rather than downstream fine-tuning, treat this as a prototype idea: use training signals instead of static data features to select synthetic data. Before scaling it up, the open questions are compute overhead, gradient approximation quality, and whether the real-gradient anchor remains meaningful under multi-domain mixed training.1a:T605,This is a product announcement rather than a technical paper, so the training recipe is not disclosed and should not be over-inferred. Still, several technical directions are visible from the full text. First, Anthropic explicitly exposes effort level as a controllable inference-budget axis and compares models using score versus cost per task across effort settings. That implies joint design of model behavior and inference policy: low effort for throughput and low cost, higher effort for longer deliberation or more steps. Second, Sonnet 5.5 is repeatedly described as using fewer output tokens, doing less unnecessary web search, asking fewer blocking questions, and batching tool calls more often. Those are usually signs of post-training that shapes agent policy rather than simple prompting: when to call tools, whether to parallelize them, when to stop gathering information, and how aggressively to compress the response. Third, the claim that it improves without changing prompts suggests the gain is not prompt-specific tuning alone; the model’s internal preferences and action priors have shifted. Fourth, the safety note says its cyber capability is now comparable to Opus 5, which triggers stronger safeguards and fallbacks. That indicates capability growth has crossed a risk threshold, and release policy is coupled to capability evaluation. From a foundation-model perspective, the interesting object is the full stack: pretraining, agentic post-training, effort-controlled inference, tool-use policy, and safety gating.1b:T510,The most striking public number is 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 for Sonnet 5.5 versus 10.3% for Sonnet 5, a very large jump. The post also states that at Medium effort, Sonnet 5.5 exceeds Sonnet 5’s best score on Terminal-Bench for less than one-tenth of the cost per task. On FrontierCode, Sonnet 5.5 at High effort matches GPT-6 Sol’s best score at roughly one-fifth of the cost per task, and is 10 points above Sonnet 5 at the same effort while costing about one-fifteenth as much per task. On CursorBench, Sonnet 5.5 at Low effort beats Sonnet 5’s best score for under one-tenth of the cost, and its best score is within about two points of Opus 5.5. On AA-Briefcase, a long-horizon knowledge-work benchmark, Sonnet 5.5 at Medium effort beats Sonnet 5’s best score at about one-ninth of the cost. On GDPval-AA, it is only two points below Opus 5.5 and roughly 400 points above Sonnet 5. The real-world anecdotes are also informative: across 118 app builds, Sonnet 5.5 averaged 3.6 iterations per build versus 7.7 for Opus 5; in offline Slackbot evals, it used about 14% fewer output tokens without prompt changes; in Unity’s multi-step editor and coding benchmark, it completed 90% of tasks. The common pattern is not just better answers, but faster convergence to a usable solution.1c:T4e4,Read it with attention to three things. First, focus on the score-versus-cost-per-task plots across effort levels rather than isolated benchmark numbers. The real question is how the Pareto frontier moves: whether low effort now covers capability regions that previously required much higher effort, and whether high effort still extends the ceiling. Second, pay close attention to the behavioral descriptions: batched tool calls, fewer steps, less web search, fewer output tokens, and fewer mid-build clarification questions. Those are external symptoms of changed training signals and are more informative than generic capability claims. Third, read the safety section carefully, especially why a Sonnet-tier model now needs cyber safeguards similar to stronger models. If the system card is available, prioritize the evaluation protocol, the definition of effort, the accounting of task cost, and the automated behavioral audit metrics. The most useful open questions are: how much of the cost reduction comes from token compression versus step compression; whether effort mainly increases reasoning tokens, tool calls, or search depth; and how much of the coding jump comes from stronger base-model knowledge versus more mature agent post-training.1d:T415,The method extends ELF. A frozen Qwen3-0.6B-Base encoder provides clean text states. Response states are corrupted in continuous space, and a bidirectional Transformer denoiser predicts clean states through velocity regression. The model also learns a token decoder, so the final response tokens are emitted in parallel. ELF-REG adds REPA+REG. REPA aligns intermediate denoiser states with hidden states from a frozen Qwen3-1.7B-Base AR teacher, using a learned projector and cosine loss at matching token positions. REG adds a global teacher-derived target: the last content-token state from the teacher is standardized, corrupted, and denoised as an extra token. This token exchanges information with text through self-attention and receives velocity-regression and REPA supervision. At inference time, the teacher and projector are removed; text states and the REG token start from noise, and only text is decoded. The paper also studies early stopping by decoding intermediate clean predictions before the full denoising trajectory finishes.1e:T747,MoSAR, short for Mixture of Semantic Attention Regimes, inserts a lightweight router on the post-RoPE Q/K pathway. The router is bilinear and conditions on both queries and keys, rather than routing only one side. That choice is important: routing only queries gives row-wise structure, and routing only keys gives column-wise structure, but neither can localize useful two-dimensional regions of the attention matrix before dense similarities are computed. With both sides routed, the interaction between token i and token j selects a regime.

Each semantic regime defines a distance gate g(d). The gate is not just a simple exponential decay. It has a near-distance plateau where RoPE interactions are largely preserved, a transition region with smooth attenuation, and a low-relevance region where interactions become small enough to approximate away. This avoids the semantic discontinuity of hard local masks and makes approximability an outcome of the learned geometry.

The routing is input-conditioned and applied after positional encoding, so regime selection depends on contextual token representations that already carry positional structure. That is why the paper uses the term semantic regimes: locality is not determined by distance alone. MoSAR-Cost adds an explicit pressure toward shorter expected reach, biasing the router toward cheaper regimes and turning the quality-efficiency trade-off into a trainable objective.

Relative to prior efficient attention methods, the differences are clear. It does not predefine a sparse pattern; it predefines a set of decay laws and lets the data choose among them. It does not start by deleting edges; it first learns continuous attenuation and then exploits low-value regions for approximation. And it treats efficient attention as a geometry-learning problem rather than only an operator-design problem.1f:T5f3,The main study uses 500M-parameter models trained from scratch and compares dense RoPE, fixed-locality baselines, MoSAR, and the cost-aware MoSAR-Cost. The headline result is that adaptive controlled decay outperforms both dense RoPE and fixed locality among the evaluated variants at 4096 and 8192 tokens, with MoSAR achieving the best perplexity in those long-context settings. The gains appear to be concentrated where long-range structure matters, which is aligned with the method’s goal.

The more interesting result is the inference-time approximation study. The authors replace soft mixture routing with deterministic top-1 routing at inference, effectively discretizing the learned geometry. This substantially reduces expected normalized reach while keeping perplexity competitive under length extrapolation. That suggests the learned regimes are not merely a training-time regularizer; they induce a geometry that can be compressed into a cheaper routing policy. MoSAR-Cost pushes the trade-off further toward lower reach, with some language-modeling cost, making the quality-versus-compute curve explicit rather than reporting a single operating point.

The most useful ablations are likely the ones on one-sided versus two-sided routing, number of regimes, the role of smooth transition regions, strength of cost regularization, and extrapolation behavior. The key question is not only whether perplexity improves, but whether perplexity, reach, and approximation error move in a stable and interpretable way.20:T412,Start with the introduction and lock onto the paper’s reframing: the target is not a better hand-designed sparse pattern, but a learned decay geometry over attention interactions. Then go to the method section and focus on three pieces: the definition of a semantic regime, the bilinear query-key router, and the MoSAR-Cost objective. It is worth understanding why routing is applied after RoPE rather than before it.

In the experiments, prioritize figures and tables that show perplexity across context lengths, expected or normalized reach, and the gap between soft mixture routing and deterministic top-1 routing. If time is limited, try to answer three questions: do the learned regimes actually separate into different locality behaviors, do those behaviors vary with layer and token semantics, and is the inference-time discretization loss small enough to matter in practice. Around 35 to 50 minutes should be enough for a solid skim. For replication judgment, the appendix on implementation details and extra ablations is necessary.21:T421,The analysis has three parts. First, it characterizes the population-optimal UDM predictor. Because uniform corruption mixes preserved tokens and random vocabulary tokens, every subset of observed positions defines a hypothesis about which context tokens are reliable. Time does not create new hypotheses; it reweights them through the noise level, with a signal-to-noise quantity such as rho_t = K alpha_t / (1 - alpha_t) controlling how much the observed context should be trusted. Second, the work studies the empirical finite-data oracle. In language data, the discrete sequence space is huge, and training examples are typically far apart. A corrupted sequence therefore remains closer to its original clean sequence than to competing examples over most noise levels, causing the posterior to concentrate and reducing the effect of time-dependent reweighting. Third, it derives a bound linking empirical time sensitivity to a post-corruption separation margin. The bound weakens near the high-noise endpoint, where multiple hypotheses become plausible.22:T4d5,LAVOIR builds on the Laya/Jev interface for typed decisions. The original input contains the question type, instruction, option markers, and the state. LAVOIR appends a slot block for candidate missing information. A single forward pass returns both the decision distribution and a predicted VOI score for each slot. The model keeps Laya’s ModernBERT-large decision head and adds a zero-initialized segment embedding so that, when no slots are present, the logits match Laya exactly in fp32. The VOI head reads each slot representation together with features of the current decision distribution and predicts a scalar value. It is a small MLP with about 0.27M parameters, LayerNorm, a 256-unit GELU hidden layer, and a scalar output. A Gini-based cap constrains the predicted value by the maximum expected gain of a calibrated posterior, which prevents the model from over-asking when it is already confident. Training labels are produced without human annotation: schema rules define the gold decision for complete profiles, an LLM verbalizes messages and answers, exact posteriors are computed by enumeration, and realized gains are measured as the increase in the model probability assigned to the gold decision after asking a slot.23:T4bf,The method defines a Spectral Concentration Ratio over each pretrained weight matrix: the energy in the leading 10% singular directions is compared against the remaining spectrum, with regularization for small or rank-deficient cases. This concentration score is combined with the Frobenius norm to rank residual units by an offline sensitivity proxy. Each scheduled unit receives a lifetime. Before the lifetime expires, its residual branch is evaluated normally; after that, the executor reuses the cached residual-branch update from the latest refresh. A key design choice is that the method does not cache a stale full hidden state. The current upstream residual stream continues to flow through the identity path, and only the branch increment is reused. Dependency-coupled operations are grouped into atomic units. The perturbation analysis motivates the score for pre-norm Transformer attention and MLP branches by connecting spectral quantities to local Lipschitz-style sensitivity bounds. The authors explicitly limit this argument: drift along the diffusion trajectory, downstream amplification, AdaLN, U-shaped skips, cross-attention, and convolutional components are not fully captured by weights alone.24:T8f8,方法由三个互补部件组成，全部是 training-free 的推理改造。

第一部分是 Token-Sparse Updates。作者先分析相邻 loop 之间 hidden state 的变化，发现后期只有少量 token 仍然发生显著更新，而且活跃 token 集合近似嵌套：后一轮还在变化的 token，大多是前一轮活跃 token 的子集。基于这个现象，FlashLoop 只对“活跃 token”重算 block，并为这些 token 生成新的 K/V；已经收敛的 token 直接复用上一轮状态和 KV。这样做同时减少了前向计算和跨 loop KV 存储。这里的关键不是静态剪枝，而是按 loop 动态决定哪些 token 继续更新。

第二部分是 Sparse Attention。作者观察到 attention output 的跨 loop 变化，主要由少数 attention columns 决定，也就是少量 key/value 位置主导了相邻 loop 的差异。这些重要列在相邻 loop 间还有较强稳定性，因此可以用前一轮的 attention-contribution 统计来预测下一轮需要重点计算的 key 集合。为了避免只在子集上做 softmax 带来的尺度偏移，方法还缓存全局概率质量，用来校正 sparse softmax 的归一化尺度。这个设计说明作者不是简单做 top-k attention，而是在尽量保留 full-softmax 数值语义的前提下近似跨 loop 增量。

第三部分是 KV-Residual Quantization。作者没有直接把每一轮完整 KV 都低比特量化，而是把某一轮作为 base state，再存相邻 loop 的低比特 residual。原因是实验显示相邻 loop 的 KV 残差比分别独立的完整 KV 更容易量化，在相同 bit-width 下重建误差更低。这一点很合理：循环 refinement 后，相邻状态差值分布更集中、更低熵。于是 KV cache 变成“量化基底 + 低比特残差”的形式，进一步压缩显存。

实现层面，论文强调这是 loop-native inference framework，而不是三个独立 trick 的拼接。作者做了 GPU 侧的 pipeline 和 kernel 优化，使 token 稀疏更新、稀疏 attention、残差量化能协同工作，避免稀疏带来的 kernel launch 和 gather/scatter 开销把理论收益吃掉。这个系统视角是论文成立的关键，因为 looped model 的瓶颈本来就不只在 FLOPs，还在 KV 带宽和长上下文内存。25:T923,FlashLoop is a training-free inference framework built from three coordinated components.

The first is Token-Sparse Updates. The authors analyze hidden-state changes between adjacent loops and show that, as recurrence proceeds, only a small subset of tokens still changes substantially. Moreover, the active-token sets are approximately nested: tokens that remain active in a later loop are mostly a subset of those active in the previous one. FlashLoop therefore recomputes the Transformer block only for active tokens and reuses hidden states and KV states for tokens that have effectively converged. This reduces both compute and the need to maintain a full per-loop KV cache.

The second is Sparse Attention. The paper shows that cross-loop changes in attention outputs are dominated by a sparse subset of attention columns, meaning a small number of key/value positions account for most of the difference between adjacent loops. These important columns are relatively stable across loops, so FlashLoop predicts them using attention-contribution statistics from the previous loop. To avoid the scale mismatch that usually appears when softmax is computed on a subset, the method caches global probability mass to preserve the normalization scale of the full softmax. This is more careful than a generic top-k attention approximation; it is tailored to incremental cross-loop updates.

The third is KV-Residual Quantization. Instead of quantizing each loop’s full KV states independently, FlashLoop stores a quantized base state plus low-bit residuals between adjacent loops. The motivation is empirical: adjacent-loop KV residuals are easier to quantize than full KV tensors, yielding lower reconstruction error under the same bit budget. That matches the intuition that iterative refinement makes successive states highly correlated and low-entropy in difference space.

A key part of the paper is that these are not presented as isolated tricks. The system is implemented with GPU-aware pipelining and optimized kernels so that token sparsity, sparse attention, and residual quantization work together without losing the gains to irregular memory access or kernel overhead. That systems angle is essential because the bottleneck in looped inference is not just FLOPs, but also KV bandwidth and memory footprint under long context.26:T5ee,The motivating numbers are striking. On a single A100 with a 32K-token prompt, Ouro-2.6B with four loops takes 27 seconds for prefill, while LLaMA-3.1-8B takes 3 seconds. KV cache alone is about 48 GiB for Ouro versus 4 GiB for LLaMA. The point is clear: a smaller looped model can be much worse in latency and memory if executed in the standard dense way.

Across several looped Transformer models, FlashLoop reports up to 1.64x end-to-end speedup and up to 6x KV-cache memory reduction while largely preserving accuracy. The paper’s main message is not extreme compression at any cost, but recovering the practical efficiency that parameter sharing was supposed to provide in the first place.

The most informative experiments are the mechanism studies. Figure 2 and the appendix document three empirical regularities: token updates become increasingly sparse across loops and form approximately nested active sets; attention-output differences are concentrated in a small number of columns that can be predicted from the previous loop; and KV residuals are more quantization-friendly than full KV states under matched settings. These analyses justify why each module should work, instead of treating the speedup as a black-box engineering result.

From a research perspective, the important takeaway is not only the 1.64x number. It is the evidence that additional loop depth does not translate into fully new computation at every step; a meaningful fraction of it becomes reusable, predictable, and compressible.27:T4bd,For a skim-level read, start with the Introduction, Figure 1, and Figure 2. Then read the method subsections for the three components and finish with the main results and ablations. Around 25 to 40 minutes should be enough to capture the main ideas.

Three things deserve attention. First, look at how the paper measures cross-loop redundancy, especially token-update sparsity and the nested active-set pattern. That determines whether Token-Sparse Updates is a robust structural property or just a one-off observation. Second, inspect the normalization correction in Sparse Attention, namely how cached global probability mass is used to preserve softmax scale. If this part is weak, accuracy usually degrades quickly. Third, check the KV-residual quantization error curves and bit-width choices; that section is particularly useful for long-context inference and serving work.

Even if your main focus is pretraining rather than inference systems, there is a deeper question worth keeping in mind: why do looped models naturally exhibit lazy updates? The paper does not fully answer it, but the phenomenon may connect to iterative refinement, residual-state convergence, and stabilization of attention patterns.28:T41b,The method defines the original routed MoE output for a token as a consensus, meaning the weighted mixture to be preserved, not an assumption that experts agree. Each expert is represented through its residual relative to this consensus. For a fixed layer input, RAZOR derives an exact single-deletion identity for the local output change. The identity accounts for survivor weight renormalization and, when applicable, router-selected refill that promotes an unselected expert into the active set. Without refill, the deletion shift depends on the deviation between the removed expert output and the consensus, scaled by its routing weight; this already shows why gate mass and output norm are insufficient. With refill, the promoted expert’s residual can compensate for or amplify the removed contribution. RAZOR runs only forward passes on calibration tokens, aggregates local deletion damage per expert within each layer, and prunes the most replaceable experts under the target budget. It avoids gradients, subset search, and recovery training.29:T4dd,The paper uses a roofline-style analysis to separate weight traffic from KV-cache traffic during decode. For a model with P parameters and weight width wp, a batch-one decode step performs roughly 2P FLOPs and reads P·wp bytes, giving about 1 FLOP/B for BF16 weights. An H100 SXM has a BF16 dense ridge point around 295 FLOP/B, so this regime is bandwidth-bound by a large margin. KV attention has the same structure: one query attending over s cached tokens costs about 4sdh FLOPs per head and reads 2sdh·wkv bytes, again about 1 FLOP/B in BF16. GQA improves reuse by the query-to-KV head group factor g, but even g=8 gives only about 8 FLOP/B, still far below the ridge point. The paper then explains why batching helps weight reads but not KV reads. Weight bytes can be amortized across requests; KV bytes cannot, because each sequence owns its cache. The techniques are organized into five mechanism classes: quantization reduces element width, token eviction reduces retained tokens, paging manages KV blocks and fragmentation, prefix caching shares common prompt prefixes, and memory tiering moves KV state across HBM, host DRAM, and storage. The paper’s comparison discipline is to keep analytical claims and measured claims separate.2a:T422,The most important quantitative examples are concrete. For Llama-3-70B in BF16, the weight footprint is about 140 GB, already larger than a single 80 GB HBM device. The KV cache size is Bkv = 2·L·nkv·dh·wkv·s. With L=80, nkv=8, dh=128, and BF16 storage, Llama-3-70B uses 327,680 KV bytes per token. A single 128k-token sequence therefore adds about 42 GB of KV state; a 1M-token sequence requires about 328 GB, more than the aggregate HBM of four 80 GB H100 devices. The arithmetic-intensity numbers are equally important: BF16 batch-one decode sits near 1 FLOP/B for weight traffic, while the H100 ridge point is about 295 FLOP/B. On the attention side, GQA with group factor 8 still reaches only about 8 FLOP/B. Weight-side batching approaches the ridge only at a batch size around 295 in this simplified model, while KV-side intensity is invariant to batch size. The paper’s measurement contribution is to make these comparisons explicit rather than mixing throughput, latency, memory footprint, and quality degradation under incompatible settings.2b:T45c,The analysis separates two mechanisms. Feedback exposure describes where quantization error is structurally dangerous. In models such as Huginn-3.5B and Recurrent-Llama, recurrence passes through a non-residual loop-entry adapter. Quantizing this adapter perturbs the recurrent state without an identity path, so the error is injected into future steps. Quantizing the residual core is much less harmful because the identity path buffers the perturbation. The paper uses the local spectral radius of the per-step Jacobian as a stability diagnostic for possible amplification directions. Calibration blindness is a different issue. GPTQ builds a Hessian proxy H=X^T X from calibration activations. If X is collected only from the first invocation of a shared layer, it can miss directions that appear in later loop steps. The paper compares this one-step calibration with trajectory calibration, which accumulates activations across all recurrent invocations. It also distinguishes per-channel INT4 from grouped INT4 with group size 128, where the latter reduces quantization error at the cost of extra scale storage.2c:T4c7,The Huginn-3.5B diagnostic is the clearest result. On 100 GSM8K examples, bf16 reaches 34% exact match, while per-channel INT4 on both the loop-entry adapter and recurrent core drops to 0%. A 50-prompt token-agreement diagnostic localizes the damage: adapter-only INT4 gives 10.5% agreement, adapter plus core gives 10.6%, and core-only INT4 keeps 87.9%. This points to the non-residual adapter as the main failure point. COCONUT behaves differently because it reuses a residual GPT-2 stack; agreement increases from 44.8% after the base forward to 61.5% after eight latent recurrences. Standard one-step sensitivity metrics fail to predict the Huginn result: small random input perturbations rank the adapter as the least sensitive among 17 projections, and Hessian trace highlights a core projection even though quantizing the adapter is far more damaging. Grouped INT4 avoids the immediate collapse, but one-step GPTQ still underperforms round-to-nearest on five of nine checkpoints. More calibration prompts do not remove the mismatch, because the missing information is the set of directions visited later in the trajectory. Linear-filter and Mamba controls show that feedback exposure is not specific to Transformers.2d:T85b,The method has three main components. First, it redefines the reusable object. Instead of caching whole requests or token prefixes, DynBranch stores a completed branch subgraph together with the exact input that triggered it and the external reads it depended on. A later request may consume the entry only if the input matches exactly and those reads are still fresh; any write to the recorded dependencies invalidates the entry. This is important for agent workflows where retrieval and tool outputs depend on mutable external state, so prompt matching alone is insufficient.

Second, it makes unresolved branches addressable. The mechanism relies on a stable coordinate provided by the workflow template: the identity of a decision point known before the branch resolves, such as a router stage or a fixed tool-selection site. Using this coordinate, the system can launch candidate branch subgraphs as fills during the resolution window. A fill is speculative execution of a candidate downstream subgraph before the actual branch is chosen. The safety rule is strict: fills remain invisible until branch selection occurs and a canonical demand authorizes their use via exact match and freshness checks. Wrong predictions therefore waste resources but do not alter semantics.

Third, DynBranch uses a two-level admission controller. One level decides whether to generate candidates at all; the second decides whether each candidate fill should run. The decision criterion is whether expected benefit exceeds a load-dependent price. That price is not a fixed threshold. It reads current decode occupancy and KV occupancy from the engine and prices work over the fill's execution horizon. This allows aggressive speculation at low load and automatic contraction at high load. The paper also indicates that the controller learns benefit estimates from delayed feedback rather than relying only on static heuristics.

Implementation-wise, DynBranch sits at the model-API boundary between agent harnesses and unmodified SGLang or vLLM backends. That makes it a serving middleware design rather than a new agent runtime or a model-side method.2e:T737,The main setup uses Qwen3-32B on 4×H200, with additional results on Qwen3-8B with an RTX 4090. The paper first motivates the problem empirically: in measured coding, research, and scientific agents, 45%–57% of end-to-end latency is downstream time serialized after model output. That establishes that the branch-resolution barrier is not a corner case.

On performance, DynBranch reduces mean latency by up to 32% relative to the strongest prior system for each workload on the same GPUs, and by 46%–66% relative to a no-reuse floor. When reuse is disabled and only early fill is kept, mean latency still drops by 8.5%–34.4% on model-driven paths, and user-turn latency drops by 46.6%–47.7% in human-interaction settings. This is an important result: the gains do not come only from cross-request reuse; overlapping work during the branch-resolution window already matters.

The experimental structure also suggests three points worth checking closely. First is correctness: the paper states that workflow results are preserved, consistent with the design where speculative fills become visible only after canonical authorization. Second is load sensitivity: the two-level controller should show different admission behavior under different occupancy regimes, otherwise the claim of safe speculation under load would be weak. Third is generality: the authors report that benefits persist across backbone families, which suggests the effect comes from workflow structure and serving dynamics rather than a model-specific artifact.

The provided text does not include the full result tables, so it is not safe to invent more workload-level absolute latency or hit-rate numbers. But the central empirical message is clear: the combination of reuse, early fill, and load-aware admission outperforms caching-only or speculation-only baselines.2f:T525,The framework maximizes draft-token acceptance subject to an f-divergence constraint between the mentored output distribution and the target distribution. The total-variation case is used as a warm-up and has a clean geometric structure: the set of optimal solutions is the intersection of a coordinate-wise hyperrectangle induced by the drafter and target, the probability simplex, and the active divergence boundary. This set is large enough to contain the optimal solutions for all strictly convex f-divergences. For a general strictly convex f-divergence, the optimal mentored distribution is unique and has a coordinate-wise clamping form, π* = max{αq, min{p, βq}}, where q is the target distribution, p is the drafter distribution, and 0 ≤ α < 1 < β. Intuitively, each token probability is kept within lower and upper multiplicative bands around the target probability, while moving along a one-dimensional path from the target toward the drafter. A notable property is that this path does not depend on the chosen f-divergence. The paper further connects the composite output distribution to boosting by developing a multiclass extension of self-normalized boosting and by showing how the drafter-target mixture can satisfy boosting-style conditions when the two models have useful edge complementarity.30:T4fb,The method, PISA, builds a coarse-to-fine pyramid over key blocks. The finest level contains fixed-size blocks, and each coarser level is formed by pooling adjacent lower-level representations. Instead of scoring every fine-grained block, routing starts at the coarsest level. At each level, the query computes LogSumExp scores over only a bounded candidate set, keeps the Top-K candidates, and expands those selected blocks into their children at the next finer level. This repeats until the leaf blocks are reached.

With a fixed branching factor, Top-K budget, and leaf block size, each query evaluates only a bounded number of candidates per level, and the number of levels is O(log N). That gives O(log N) routing per query and O(N log N) routing over the sequence. The final sparse attention is then computed over the selected original blocks.

The practical angle is important here. The authors implement hardware-aware Triton kernels that fuse multi-level routing and LSE scoring, so intermediate candidates do not need to be repeatedly materialized and moved through memory. They also avoid constructing a dense query-key score matrix. That matters because many sparse-attention ideas fail to deliver real speedups once kernel and memory traffic are taken seriously.31:T91f,方法核心是 acoustic-to-text KV compression。基础模型是 MiniCPM-o 4.5，它按 1 秒为单位处理 duplex unit，每个 unit 内包含音频 token、一个 native 的 <|listen|> 或 <|speak|> 决策，以及后续可能的响应生成。作者在每个 unit 的第一个 native decision 之后，插入一个可选的 transcription segment，用新引入的 <|asr_start|> 和 <|asr_end|> 包围。这个 segment 只作为语言模型上下文中的文本记忆存在，不送入 speech decoder，也不会被说出来。

推理时，模型自己决定是否打开 side channel。如果预测出 <|asr_start|>，就贪心解码最多 64 个文本 token，直到 <|asr_end|>；若超长或遇到控制 token，则强制闭合。随后，当 resident KV cache 超过目标预算时，系统驱逐更早的 acoustic states，但保留这些 transcript token，并保留一个最近的 acoustic window 以覆盖转写延迟。于是，较老的语音内容以文本形式留在上下文里，最近一段仍保留原始声学细节，形成“远处文本化、近处声学化”的混合记忆。

训练上，作者没有单独接一个 ASR 模型，而是复用原有 LM backbone，只用 LoRA 适配 side channel。监督信号来自带词级强制对齐的转写数据：每个词根据其声学结束时间和额外延迟 δ 被分配到某个 1 秒 unit 中，每个词只出现在一个目标 transcription segment。仅用 transcription cross-entropy 会改变原模型的原生对话行为，所以作者再加入 token-level knowledge distillation。具体做法是：冻结原始 full-duplex 模型作为 teacher，让它在同一音频上、但不插入 transcription segment 地运行；收集 teacher 在所有 native prediction positions 的全词表分布；student 在插入 transcription segment 的序列上训练时，对这些 native 位置同时拟合 teacher 分布。这样 side channel 学会转写，同时尽量不扰动原有 listen/speak 决策、停顿处理、打断响应等行为。

这个设计和“单独训练一个流式 ASR，再把文本喂回模型”相比，有两个差异。其一，推理时不需要额外 ASR 模块，部署更简单；其二，蒸馏约束的是 full-duplex 原生行为，而不只是转写准确率，因此目标更贴近语音对话模型的系统需求。32:T828,实验围绕三件事展开：KV 峰值控制、长时语音理解、实时性与交互行为保持。主模型是 MiniCPM-o 4.5。作者指出，转写后的文本记忆大约每秒只占 3 个序列位置，而原始 acoustic history 约占 17 个位置，这给压缩上限提供了直观背景。

在十分钟 LongSpeech session 上，与“同样经过 side-channel 适配但不做 eviction”的模型相比，峰值 streaming KV cache 大小下降 64.6%。这说明收益主要来自“文本化后驱逐旧声学 KV”，而不是仅仅插入 transcript token。长时理解方面，论文称该方法在 transcription、temporal question answering、summarization 上都优于 native streaming，说明文本记忆不仅节省显存，也改善了对长程语言内容的保持。

实时性方面，在 4K KV cache budget 下，包含 transcription 与 cache eviction 在内的整套处理，在 H100、batch size 1 上对每个 1 秒音频单元平均耗时 461 ms；在 10,039 个 unit 的测量中没有 deadline miss。这一点很关键，因为方法成立的前提就是 side channel 能在 listening-time slack 内完成。若超过 1 秒窗口，就会破坏 full-duplex 实时性。

行为保持方面，Full-Duplex-Bench 上 pause-handling、turn-taking、interruption 等指标与原模型相当，支持了蒸馏约束确实在抑制 side-channel 训练对原生交互行为的扰动。摘要还提到 WER 统计会把 skipped/truncated segments 计入错误，这意味着作者没有通过只评估成功打开 side channel 的片段来美化结果。

从方法设计推断，值得关注的消融应包括：只做 CE 转写监督、不做 KD 时 native behavior 的退化；不同 KV budget 下理解与实时性的折中；recent acoustic window 大小对性能的影响；以及 emission delay δ 对转写完整性和驱逐时机的影响。给出的全文片段没有完整表格数字，但主结论已经足够明确：在线文本化旧语音上下文，可以在不破坏 full-duplex 交互的前提下显著降低峰值 KV，并提升长时理解。33:T95a,The core method is acoustic-to-text KV compression. The base model, MiniCPM-o 4.5, processes interaction in 1-second duplex units. Each unit contains audio tokens, a native <|listen|> or <|speak|> decision, and possibly response generation. After the first native decision in each unit, the authors insert an optional transcription segment delimited by two new tokens, <|asr_start|> and <|asr_end|>. This segment stays in the language-model context as textual memory, but it is excluded from the speech decoder input and from spoken output.

At inference time, the model decides whether to open the side channel. If it predicts <|asr_start|>, it greedily decodes up to 64 text tokens until <|asr_end|>; if the segment overruns or hits a control token, the segment is forcibly closed. When the resident KV cache exceeds a target budget, older acoustic states are evicted while transcript tokens are retained, together with a recent acoustic window that covers transcription delay. The resulting memory is hybrid: older context is preserved in text form, while recent context remains acoustically grounded.

Training avoids a separate ASR model. The side channel is adapted with LoRA on top of the existing LM backbone. Supervision comes from transcribed utterances with word-level forced alignment. Each word is assigned to a 1-second unit based on its acoustic endpoint plus an additional emission delay delta, and each word appears in exactly one target transcription segment. However, pure transcription cross-entropy would alter the model's native conversational behavior. To prevent that, the paper adds token-level knowledge distillation. A frozen teacher, namely the original full-duplex model without transcription segments, processes the same audio. Its full-vocabulary distributions at native prediction positions are collected, and the student is trained to match them at those positions while also learning the inserted transcription segments. This constrains changes to native listen/speak decisions, pause handling, interruption behavior, and response generation.

Compared with a pipeline that runs a separate streaming ASR and feeds text back into the model, this design has two practical differences. It removes the need for an extra ASR module at inference, and it regularizes the adapted model toward preserving full-duplex behavior rather than optimizing transcription alone.34:T989,The experiments focus on three aspects: peak KV control, long-form speech understanding, and real-time behavioral preservation. The base model is MiniCPM-o 4.5. The paper notes that transcript memory uses roughly 3 sequence positions per second of speech, versus about 17 for acoustic history, which gives a clear intuition for why the compression can matter.

On 10-minute LongSpeech sessions, peak streaming KV cache size is reduced by 64.6% relative to the same side-channel-adapted model without eviction. This is an important comparison because it isolates the gain from converting old acoustic context into text and then evicting acoustic KV, rather than from simply inserting transcript tokens. On long-form understanding, the method improves transcription, temporal question answering, and summarization over native streaming, suggesting that textual memory is not only cheaper but also more effective for retaining long-range linguistic content.

On real-time feasibility, under a 4K KV-cache budget the full processing path, including transcription and cache eviction, averages 461 ms per 1-second audio unit on an H100 at batch size 1. Across 10,039 measured units, there are no deadline misses. This matters because the whole method depends on finishing side-channel work within the listening-time slack.

On behavioral preservation, results on Full-Duplex-Bench show comparable pause handling, turn taking, and interruption performance. That supports the claim that token-level distillation successfully constrains the side-channel adaptation. The paper also states that skipped or truncated transcription segments are counted as errors in WER, which is a useful detail because it avoids reporting only successful side-channel openings.

The most informative ablations are likely the following: cross-entropy-only transcription training versus CE plus KD, to show how native behavior degrades without distillation; different KV budgets to expose the trade-off between memory and understanding; the size of the retained recent acoustic window; and the effect of the emission delay delta on transcription completeness and eviction timing. The provided text does not include all tables, so it would be unsafe to add more exact numbers, but the main result is already clear: online textualization of old speech context can substantially reduce peak KV while preserving full-duplex interaction and improving long-range understanding.35:T57d,This is a skim-to-light-read paper, especially if you care about speech LMs, unified memory, or streaming multimodal inference. Start with the Introduction to set the boundary correctly: the goal is not better ASR, but online memory compression inside a full-duplex speech LM. Then read the method section carefully, focusing on where the transcription segment is inserted, how the side channel is opened during inference, and how eviction is triggered. Those details determine whether the approach is actually deployable without changing the backbone architecture.

The training section is worth extra attention. In particular, look at how forced alignment assigns words to units and how token-level KD is applied only at native prediction positions. That is the most technically interesting part, because it explains why LoRA adaptation can add transcription ability without noticeably damaging native listening and speaking behavior.

In the experiments, prioritize the tables on peak KV usage, LongSpeech understanding tasks, and Full-Duplex-Bench behavior preservation. If there is a latency timeline or a budget sweep, read that too, since it directly shows engineering feasibility. Around 30–40 minutes should be enough for the key ideas. If you only want to judge transferability to another speech LM, read the method figure, the training objective, and the real-time result under the 4K budget.36:T4ad,The study uses three settings. E1 measures spontaneous reward hacking: 17 language models each receive one full sandboxed terminal-agent attempt on each of 38 tasks, without being instructed or authorized to hack. An attempt is a complete ReAct-style agent session, not a single model response. The agent can inspect files, call tools, run the visible scorer, edit its solution, and resubmit until a 40-turn or 3600-second limit. The reported evidence suggests that overall model rankings are more stable than individual answers and domain-level profiles.39:T457,The method uses a closed-testing construction. An independent proposal split nominates one candidate-specific floor c_k for each policy. A fresh certification split then runs an exact binomial test for H_k: P(S_k < c_k) ≥ α. Rejecting this null certifies that the candidate’s lower α-quantile is at least the proposed floor. Holm’s step-down procedure controls the family-wise error rate at δ across candidates. The selected policy is the certified candidate with the largest floor; the procedure abstains if no certified floor exceeds a predeclared operating threshold. The guarantee allows arbitrary within-unit dependence across candidates, such as correlated judge scores on the same prompt, while requiring i.i.d. evaluation units. Compared with matched-proposal Bonferroni, Holm gives a uniformly stronger rejection set on every dataset. Compared with exact COPS, it certifies a different statistical object, so uniform dominance is not claimed. The score map s_k is treated as a fixed measurable function; it need not be unbiased, Gaussian, asymptotically normal, or a mean off-policy estimator.3a:T48b,The study attempted 10 open model variants across five families and a scale range from 8B to 675B parameters. Eight met the inclusion threshold: gemma3:12b, gpt-oss:20b, gpt-oss:120b, ministral-3:8b, mistral-large-3:675b, minimax-m2.1, minimax-m2.7, and qwen3-coder-next. deepseek-v3.1:671b produced no successful logged inference, likely due to client timeout, but the model was retired before the cause could be established. glm-4.7 had five successful runs across two prompts and was excluded only because it fell below the three-prompt threshold. Under bootstrap, only the bottom of the ranking remains firm; the full ordered table does not.3b:T84a,方法由三部分组成。第一部分是 PB-CSTE 环境。它是一个刻意简化、确定性的 stateful tool-use 环境，任务通过 allowlisted 的 create/update/delete/restore/goal-revision 操作修改带类型的实体。环境记录时间戳、actor class、state diff 和 snapshot，便于可执行回放与归因审计。作者主动去掉网络、并发、权限系统、随机失败和开放式浏览，这样做不是为了贴近真实世界，而是为了把“评测器是否被历史状态欺骗”这个因果问题单独拎出来。

第二部分是双向量认证。对每条轨迹，私有 certifier 构造两个向量：一个是最终时刻哪些 goal predicates 为真，对应 current-state progress；另一个是这些已满足谓词里，哪些应按事件日志规则归因给 agent，对应 agent-attributed progress。pair eligibility 要求 honest 轨迹 H 和 adversarial 轨迹 A 在这两个向量上逐项相等。这样控制住了两件事：终态真实进展相同，且可归因给 agent 的进展也相同。论文把这称为 certified equal-progress。这里的归因不是一般因果归因，而是 benchmark 内部标准化的事件日志归因规则，目的是让比较可执行、可审计。

第三部分是两类 stress protocol。其一是 equal-progress pair：在相同认证进展下，若 evaluator 给 A 更高分，则说明 evaluator 奖励了历史峰值、状态 churn、重建实体或归因歧义。其二是 strict rollback：从 honest 轨迹出发，执行一个合法逆操作，要求 active goal 不变且 current-state progress 严格下降。如果 evaluator 对 rollback 不敏感，就说明它对真实进展损失不够敏感。

理论上，作者给了两个命题。命题1说明，任何只依赖最终认证状态与认证归因的 evaluator，在 matched pair 上都应满足零膨胀。命题2说明，任何取历史最大值的 evaluator，都可能在终态相同的情况下被 adversarial witness 拉高分数。这个形式化很朴素，但足够把“current-state evaluator”和“historical evaluator”的差别说清楚。3c:T7e5,实验在 PB-CSTE v1.0 上做，包含 6 个开发任务和 18 个 sealed held-out 任务，任务类型覆盖 persistent multi-step、CRUD、fixed-goal interaction 和 GoalPatch。每个任务有 3 到 5 个持久 goal predicates，honest progress 覆盖从 1/4 到 3/4 的七个层级。最终在 18 个 held-out 任务中，历史目标运行成功构造出 15 个 canonical equal-progress adversaries。

核心结果有三组。第一组是历史式评分器的脆弱性。historical scoring 的平均 inflation 为 0.252，条件攻击成功数为 10/15，端到端 yield 为 10/18；在 rollback 检测上是 0/14，几乎完全失效。这说明只要评分器把历史上达到过的里程碑也算分，就很容易被合法 witness 利用。

第二组是语义 judge 的迁移表现。一个 structured DeepSeek judge 把 transfer inflation 降到 0.022，并能检测 10/14 个 rollback，明显比纯历史式规则好，但仍非零，说明语义 judge 即使更强，也会被定向构造的 witness 诱导。Independent-Decomposition Judge（IDJ）从任务说明中构造冻结 checklist，不访问 Oracle schema，得到 mean transfer inflation 0.017、ASR 1/15、rollback detection 12/14。这个结果说明，只要 checklist 真正锚定终态分解，而不是追踪历史痕迹，哪怕不直接访问私有 schema，也能接近 current-state 规则。

第三组是正控制。current-state rules 在该环境里达到零 inflation，并检测全部 rollback。论文解释得很清楚：PB-CSTE 中公开的 CSPS 组件与私有 certified state 一一对应，Lightweight CAPE 还额外用对应 attribution 组件，因此它们是结构性正控制，不是开放世界下的通用解法。

值得注意的实验细节是，作者还做了 replay audit，确认 15 个 canonical pair 的状态向量和归因向量确实完全匹配；并区分了 witness construction、inflation、coverage、transfer 和 rollback sensitivity 这些不同维度，而不是只报一个攻击成功率。3d:T869,The method has three layers. First, the authors build PB-CSTE, a deterministic stateful tool-use environment designed for causal isolation. Tasks operate over typed entities through allowlisted create, update, delete, restore, and goal-revision actions. Every successful operation logs timestamps, actor class, state diffs, and snapshots. The environment intentionally excludes networking, concurrency, permissions, stochastic failures, and open-ended browsing. That simplification is deliberate: the goal is to isolate evaluator failure modes, not to mimic the full messiness of real-world agents.

Second, they define dual-vector certification. For each trusted terminal state, a private certifier constructs a state vector indicating which goal predicates hold at termination, and an attribution vector indicating which satisfied predicates receive standardized agent credit under an event-log rule. A pair is eligible only if the honest trajectory H and adversarial trajectory A match component-wise on both vectors. This controls both final retained progress and credited progress. The attribution rule is not presented as general causal attribution; it is a benchmark-internal standardization that makes the comparison executable and auditable.

Third, they introduce two stress protocols. Equal-progress pairs test invariance: if an evaluator gives A a higher score than H despite identical certified progress, the extra score must come from historical peaks, churn, recreated entities, or attribution ambiguity. Strict rollback tests sensitivity: starting from H, apply a legal inverse transition that lowers certified current-state progress while keeping the active goal fixed. If the evaluator fails to penalize rollback, it is not tracking actual progress loss.

The formal section is simple but useful. Proposition 1 shows that any evaluator depending only on certified final state and certified attribution must have zero inflation on matched pairs. Proposition 2 shows that historical-max evaluators can be exploited whenever the adversarial trajectory reaches a higher intermediate peak, even if the final certified vectors are identical.3e:T813,Experiments use PB-CSTE v1.0 with 6 development tasks and 18 sealed held-out tasks, spanning persistent multi-step tasks, CRUD tasks, fixed-goal interactions, and GoalPatch cases. Each task has 3 to 5 persistent goal predicates, and honest prefixes cover seven progress levels from 1/4 to 3/4. On the 18 held-out tasks, the historical-target procedure successfully constructs 15 canonical equal-progress adversaries.

The main result is the weakness of historical scoring. Historical scoring shows mean inflation of 0.252, conditional attack success on 10/15 matched pairs, end-to-end yield of 10/18, and rollback detection of 0/14. In other words, once the evaluator rewards historical milestones, legal witnesses can often inflate the score without increasing certified final progress.

The second result concerns semantic judges. A structured DeepSeek judge reduces transfer inflation to 0.022 and detects 10/14 rollbacks. That is much better than purely historical rules, but still not zero. An Independent-Decomposition Judge (IDJ), which builds frozen checklists from task instructions without access to the private Oracle schema, achieves mean transfer inflation of 0.017, attack success 1/15, and rollback detection 12/14. This is an important finding: a judge can get close to current-state behavior if its checklist is anchored to final-state decomposition rather than historical traces, even without direct access to the certifier schema.

The positive controls are current-state rules. In PB-CSTE they achieve zero inflation and detect all rollbacks. The paper is careful here: these are structural positive controls because public CSPS components map one-to-one to the private certified state components in this benchmark. That does not mean the same solution transfers unchanged to open-world agent evaluation.

A useful experimental detail is that the authors separately report witness construction, inflation, coverage, transfer, and rollback sensitivity, and they replay-audit all 15 canonical pairs to verify exact equality of the certified vectors.3f:T428,For a quick read, start with the introduction and Figure 1. After that, read Proposition 1 and Proposition 2 to understand the clean separation between current-state evaluators and historical evaluators. The right reading stance is narrow: this paper demonstrates a controlled failure mode and a clean stress-test protocol, not a complete solution for open-world tool-agent evaluation.40:T50d,The intervention study uses 2,522 questions over 227 long videos and reports 60,008 runs across three agent architectures: Video-R1, VideoMind, and EVA. Existing benchmark scores provide unstable diagnostics: upstream capability scores do not reliably predict hallucination, and even benchmarks assigned to the same stage can move in opposite directions. The causal interventions are clearer. Replacing a length-matched random window with the oracle evidence span improves accuracy by about 17–18 points across all three architectures, roughly four times the effect of substantial frame corruption in the Watching stage. Deployed grounders recover only about one quarter of this available gain. Dilating the oracle span by up to 8x causes little loss, suggesting that overlap metrics such as mIoU can be poorly aligned with downstream usefulness. Incorrect evidence is more harmful than missing evidence: agents tolerate severe frame omission better than plausible but wrong frames from elsewhere in the video. Evidence-level diagnosis finds that 42–65% of correct answers can be unsupported by the video, and some hallucination metrics saturate under domain shift.41:T432,RECLAIM contains 100 reproduction tasks built from NeurIPS 2025 papers. Each task pins one match target before any agent run: the cheapest reported configuration that still supports the paper’s central empirical claim, together with the metric, reported value, evaluation scope, and success tolerance. Tasks are stratified by released artifacts. Run-tier papers provide code, data, and weights. Retrain-tier papers lack weights, so the agent must train the model. Reimplement-tier papers lack code, so the agent must implement the method from the paper. The benchmark does not provide scripted pipelines or prepared environments. Agents must plan the reproduction, install software, resolve dependency failures, manage GPU allocations, and produce execution evidence. Scoring is based on logs and outputs rather than the agent’s own narrative, using a separate language-model grader to audit whether the run supports the pinned claim. The benchmark is designed to be rebuilt yearly from new conference papers, which helps reduce quick saturation of a fixed static suite.42:T417,The reported success rates are low across all tiers. DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the strongest evaluated agent, reproduces 41% of Run-tier papers, 27% of Retrain-tier papers, and 12% of Reimplement-tier papers. Muse Spark 1.2 reaches 15% on Reimplement-tier, the best result for that tier. A notable finding is that Run-tier remains difficult despite providing all major artifacts. On Retrain-tier, the strongest agent reaches a verified partial result or better in 67% of runs, while the weakest reaches 27%, suggesting that partial reproduction emerges before exact recovery of the reported number. Full recovery is the harder barrier: across four agents at Retrain-tier, success stays between 15% and 27% despite a 1.7x spread in mean audit score. Compute is not the main explanation. In the 96 H100-hour budget band, 48 cells spend only 6.2% of their allocated compute on average, and only one reproduces its claim. The failure analysis attributes most failures to a small set of agent mistakes; some decline with stronger agents, while others persist.43:T8bf,论文建立了一个固定 cohort 的 repeated evaluation 框架。共有 M 个任务，每个任务预先规划 L 条重复路径，总共 N=ML 条路径；每条路径最多消耗 K 次模型响应或完整 agent episode。路径的结果用 first decisive event index T_ir 表示，若在 K 步内没有出现 decisive event，则终端标签 Y_ir=1，否则为 0。目标不是未来任务分布上的泛化均值，而是这个预先固定评测网格的经验均值 θ_C，并要求对任意可能实现的 cohort 都有 coverage 保证，也就是 fixed-cohort honest inference。

核心理论结果是两条 certification law。若设计要求每个 task 至少完成一条路径，也就是 task coverage 不能缺失，则最优最坏情形区间宽度阶为 Θ([M(t+1)]^{-1/2})；若允许省掉部分 task，把预算集中到少数任务的更多重复上，则最优阶变为 Θ([M(t+√M)]^{-1/2})。这里 t 可以理解为在覆盖每个 task 之后额外保留出来用于 replication/certification 的预算单位。作者强调 lower bound 覆盖了自适应 hard-budget policy，也就是说即便允许根据已观察结果动态调度预算，数量级上也不能突破这个界。

为了让理论可执行，论文给出固定随机子集设计和 disagreement-based certificate。直觉上，若同一 task 内计划标签高度一致，一次观测就足以把均值估得很准；但要证明这种一致性，需要额外抽样去测 disagreement。于是区间构造不只依赖 sampled mean，也显式依赖 disagreement count，形成所谓 Joint interval。这个设计比单纯把所有已观测路径当成 pooled Bernoulli 做统一推断更贴近“先覆盖任务、再花预算做认证”的实际评测流程。

论文还区分了两个目标：一个是对固定 benchmark grid 的诚实区间，另一个是对未来任务或未来运行的 population generalization。前者不需要对任务和运行结果做独立同分布假设；若要桥接到总体均值，附录里再加 Hoeffding 项。这种区分是合理的，因为很多模型发布和训练 gating 场景，真正关心的是“这次固定评测表上的分数是否足够可信”，而不是统计学意义上的外推。44:T84b,The paper formalizes repeated evaluation on a fixed cohort. There are M tasks and L planned repetition paths per task, for N = ML total paths. Each path costs at most K model responses or full agent episodes. A path outcome is represented by a first decisive-event index T_ir, and the terminal label Y_ir indicates whether no decisive event occurred within K steps. The estimand is the empirical mean over this prespecified grid, denoted theta_C, and the requirement is fixed-cohort honest coverage: the interval must be valid for every realized cohort, without assuming IID outcomes across tasks or runs.

The main theoretical contribution is a pair of sharp certification laws. If the design requires at least one completed path per task, the optimal worst-case interval width scales as Theta([M(t+1)]^{-1/2}). If omission is allowed, so some tasks may be skipped in order to spend more budget on replication elsewhere, the optimal rate becomes Theta([M(t+sqrt(M))]^{-1/2}). Here t is the extra reservation beyond the minimum needed for broad task coverage. The lower bounds apply even to adaptive hard-budget policies, so the result is not an artifact of simple non-adaptive sampling.

To make the theory operational, the paper proposes fixed random-subset designs together with disagreement-based certificates. The key idea is that when planned labels within a task agree, one observation can estimate the task contribution very well, but certifying that agreement requires extra sampling. The resulting Joint interval depends not only on the sampled mean but also on the observed disagreement count. This is more aligned with practical benchmark design than treating all observed paths as pooled Bernoulli samples.

An important conceptual distinction in the paper is between fixed-grid inference and population generalization. The primary target is the fixed benchmark grid itself, which supports honest evaluation without stochastic assumptions on task outcomes. Generalization to future tasks or runs is treated as a separate inferential objective, with an additional Hoeffding-style term discussed in the appendix.45:T532,The empirical section uses an equal-budget LiveCodeBench replay. Under the same 1100-output budget, with M = 880, t = 220, and K = 1, the paper compares the proposed Joint interval against exact pooled uniform inference. Joint produces narrower mean intervals in 15 out of 16 model panels, with a median interval-width reduction of 30.6% and a median MSE reduction of 87.0%. This supports the claim that explicitly tracking disagreement is useful in the regime where within-task agreement is common but still needs certification.

The theoretical rates are also central empirical takeaways. With mandatory task coverage, the optimal width is Theta([M(t+1)]^{-1/2}); with omission, it is Theta([M(t+sqrt(M))]^{-1/2}). The paper highlights that at zero extra reservation, the omission-enabled regime changes the attainable order from M^{-1/2} to M^{-3/4}. That is a rate-level difference, not just a constant-factor effect, and it makes task coverage a first-order design choice. The paper also studies sufficient dominance regions and controlled departures from within-task agreement to show when the finite-sample gains should be expected and when they weaken.

Because this is a theory-heavy paper, the key numbers are interval widths, MSE, and rate behavior, not benchmark score improvements in the usual model-comparison sense.46:T817,方法上这是一篇重 survey + taxonomy + protocol design 的工作。作者先把“world model”这个在文献里被混用的词拆开，区分 latent dynamics predictors、action-conditioned video predictors、large generative video models 等不同家族，避免把 Dreamer、GR-2、Sora 这类系统放在同一个模糊桶里比较。然后建立四条 evaluation lane：policy、embodied、world-model、bridge。这里 bridge 是全文最关键的概念，指那些至少尝试把预测接入控制闭环、或者显式比较 predictive branch 与 direct policy branch 的 benchmark。除了按评测模式分层，作者还按 12 类 robotic capability 做标注，把 benchmark 放到 capability × model family 的交叉表里。这样做的原因很清楚：如果只按任务名或环境名整理，仍然看不出 benchmark 到底在测什么能力，也看不出它是否有资格回答“prediction 是否有用”。

全文的核心技术产物有三块。第一块是 benchmark corpus 构建与纳入规则。作者把 benchmark 定义为可引用的 evaluation artifact，要求有明确 scoring protocol，排除纯模型、纯数据集、纯 simulator。第二块是 contrast-gap analysis。作者给出一个 advantage-of-prediction evaluation loop，要求同一 testbed 中同时运行 direct VLA 和 world-model-based policy，并报告 capability-sliced gain，而不是只给总体成功率。第三块是 actionable protocol。文中提出四个可测量量，并在 Table 9、Figure 11 里给出可承载这些测量的 testbed。虽然全文摘要没有逐项展开四个量的数学定义，但从正文脉络看，它们围绕的是：预测是否改善闭环行为、改善发生在什么能力维度、改善是否来自真正可用的 counterfactual information、以及这种改善在执行噪声和分布偏移下是否稳定。作者没有发明新的 metric 公式去替代任务成功率，而是强调需要把 prediction benefit 作为独立变量显式 instrument 起来，这一点比再造一个综合分数更稳妥。47:T433,Its value for pretraining research is not robotics per se, but the way it sharpens the link between generative objectives and downstream utility. A large part of current foundation-model work in video generation, latent dynamics, action-conditioned generation, and multimodal predictive modeling implicitly assumes that better prediction should translate into better control. The paper shows that this assumption is still weakly instrumented. That matters for anyone working on predictive pretraining or unified multimodal modeling: without advantage-aware benchmarks, gains remain trapped in proxy metrics. The quantitative picture is clear. Out of 160 benchmarks, 138 are model-agnostic, only 11 explicitly construct a VLA-versus-world-model contrast, and only 4 actually turn prediction into executed action. So the field does not lack benchmarks in volume; it lacks benchmarks designed to answer the right question. For pretraining researchers, the main lesson is that modeling quality, generation metrics, and behavioral benefit should not be treated as interchangeable.48:T76f,This is a survey built around taxonomy design and evaluation protocol design. A central move in the paper is to disambiguate the overloaded term “world model.” The authors separate latent dynamics predictors, action-conditioned video predictors, and large generative video models, instead of treating Dreamer-style systems, GR-2-like predictors, and Sora-like generators as one category. They then organize the benchmark space into four evaluation lanes: policy, embodied, world-model, and bridge. The bridge lane is the key idea. It refers to benchmarks that at least attempt to connect prediction to closed-loop control, or explicitly compare a predictive branch against a direct policy branch.

The second organizing axis is capability. Benchmarks are tagged across twelve robotic capability areas, then placed into a capability-by-model-family matrix. This is important because task names alone do not reveal what a benchmark actually measures, nor whether it can answer the “does prediction help?” question. The paper’s main technical outputs are threefold. First, a benchmark corpus with explicit inclusion rules: a benchmark must be a citable evaluation artifact with a scoring protocol, not merely a model, raw dataset, or simulator. Second, a contrast-gap analysis centered on an advantage-of-prediction evaluation loop. The proposed loop requires both a direct VLA policy and a world-model-based controller to run in the same testbed, with capability-sliced gains reported rather than only aggregate success. Third, an actionable protocol with four measurable quantities and named testbeds, presented in Table 9 and Figure 11. The paper does not try to replace task success with one new scalar metric. Instead, it argues for instrumenting prediction benefit as an explicit variable. That choice is methodologically sound: it avoids hiding the question inside another composite score.49:T587,The empirical contribution is a structured benchmark census rather than model benchmarking. The headline numbers matter. The authors catalog 160 web-verified benchmarks from 2017 to 2026 and profile them by evaluation mode, capability coverage, and model-family coverage. Among these, 138 are model-agnostic. Only 11 benchmarks, about 7%, explicitly build a VLA-versus-world-model contrast. Only 4 benchmarks actually convert prediction into executed action, which means most world-model evaluation still stops at open-loop proxies. The paper also argues that counterfactual capability is barely measured, despite the fact that imagined futures and planning are often presented as the main reason to build world models in the first place.

The most useful figures and tables are functional rather than decorative. Figures 4, 5, and 6 profile the corpus. Figures 8 and 9 provide benchmark galleries. The point is to internalize the evaluation logic: predictive modeling needs an explicit bridge from generation quality to closed-loop behavioral gain.4b:T7da,The work has three technical layers. The first is dataset construction. The authors build a benchmark of 317 manually verified knowledge reversals across medicine, law, software, and platform policy. Each case is grounded in dated official sources and includes a clear validity boundary between what used to be correct and what is correct now. This is more precise than generic knowledge-conflict datasets because the temporal transition is explicit.

The second layer is behavioral evaluation. The paper measures poisoning in a strict way: only cases where the same model is correct without retrieval but becomes wrong after seeing outdated evidence count as stale-document poisoning. That isolates the net harm introduced by retrieval. The experiments compare neutral retrieval prompts with prompts that explicitly instruct the model to follow the document, separating natural deference from instruction-amplified deference.

The third layer is temporal-applicability and internal-mechanism analysis. On 50 source-verified reversals, the authors hold the historical evidence text fixed and vary only the evaluation date. This tests whether the model changes its trust in the same evidence when it moves from valid to superseded. Models react only modestly to date changes alone, but respond much more strongly when the validity boundary is made explicit. That means the problem is not simply missing date tokens; it is a failure to map dates into applicability judgments. Causal interventions further show that information about when evidence applies can directly change the final answer, while matched control interventions do little. Attention analysis suggests that some components contribute early to this evidence-arbitration process.

The paper also evaluates a fixed hybrid reranker that combines semantic relevance, recency, and supersession cues. It reduces poisoning when metadata are reliable, showing that part of the problem can be mitigated on the retrieval side, though not fully solved there.4c:T643,The evaluation covers 12 models: six API models and six open-weight models ranging from 4B to 72B parameters. Cross-domain behavioral experiments focus on Qwen2.5 and Llama-3.1 at both small and large scales. Temporal-applicability experiments include Qwen2.5-7B/72B and Llama-3.1-8B/70B. Causal analyses focus on the 72B and 70B models.

Three result groups matter most. First, outdated retrieval flips otherwise correct answers even without explicit document-following instructions: 30% for Llama and 37% for Qwen. So the failure is not just a prompt-engineering artifact; the models already over-defer to retrieved evidence. Second, explicit instructions to follow the document raise those flip rates to 66% and 75%, showing that instruction following amplifies the selective-trust failure. Third, matched up-to-date evidence is followed almost universally, which means the models are not generally bad at using retrieval. They are bad at deciding when retrieved evidence should no longer be trusted.

The paper also finds that recent medical reversals are harder than long-established ones, suggesting that near-boundary temporal drift is especially difficult. In the fixed-evidence, changed-date setup, changing the evaluation date alone produces only limited behavioral adjustment, whereas making the validity boundary explicit causes much larger answer changes. That contrast is central because it separates date awareness from applicability reasoning. The reranker experiments show consistent reductions in poisoning when recency and supersession cues are available and metadata are trustworthy.4d:T415,This is a skim paper, but it deserves a careful skim if you work on RAG, continual pretraining, or knowledge updating.
