If you are thinking about training fixes, spend extra time on the internal-analysis section because it points directly to the missing capability: conditional trust in retrieved evidence.4e:T4fc,BAER enforces candidate symmetry through a signed-score interface: swapping the two responses should flip the sign of the judgment but preserve its magnitude, i.e. s(Tx) = -s(x). Each raw judging protocol is represented as an expert signal and decomposed into a signed preference and a candidate-invariant reliability feature. The expert bank contains nine protocols: bidirectional direct judging, self-consistency, chain-of-thought, rubric-based judging, score-then-choose, PRePair, PriDe, CalibraEval, and an internal deliberate A-versus-B expert. Experts may be run under both display orders, and probabilities are mapped back to the canonical candidate. BAER estimates each expert’s average preference probability and order instability, then builds raw and reliability-shrunk log-odds; unstable experts are downweighted. It defines three heads: evidence stacking, which combines expert signals; reliability-based routing, which selects an expert per pair using candidate-invariant reliability features; and candidate-blind reference verification, which constructs a reference without seeing either candidate and then verifies candidates against it. Development data select one head for each benchmark-backbone condition, and that choice is frozen before test evaluation.4f:T426,The paper introduces an MMORPG-style sandbox plus a curated benchmark of collaborative tasks. The simulator supports up to 1,000 concurrent agents and includes more than 380 items, 144 mob types, over 70 NPCs, and 13 high-level API tools for actions such as combat, crafting, gathering, and navigation. The high-level API design is important: it removes much of the low-level control burden so that benchmark scores reflect collaboration rather than 3D manipulation skill. The benchmark contains 100 human-annotated tasks and 100 LLM-augmented variants across combat, crafting, gathering, trading, exploration, survival, construction, and coordination. Tasks require 3 to 20 agents over 25 to 55 rounds, with asymmetric roles and no access to other agents’ internal states. The proposed Causal Collaboration Effectiveness metric builds a causal action graph over trajectories and measures the fraction of actions that contributed to the final outcome, using LLMs mainly to help infer action-level causal links rather than to issue a single subjective judgment.50:T50d,The core contribution is COMPASS, a controlled evaluation framework built from Visual Genome scene graphs. For each image, the authors sample a coherent subgraph via a random walk of up to ten steps, preserving objects, their attributes, and pairwise relations. From this shared primitive set, they generate captions with different structures and complexity levels. This enables matched comparisons between composed captions and decomposed counterparts built from the same underlying primitives. Evaluation uses a retrieval-style protocol with hard negatives designed to isolate errors in object recognition, attribute binding, and relation reasoning. On top of this setup, the paper defines two analyses. The first is the compositional integration gap: the performance difference between composed and decomposed captions under matched perturbations, intended to measure the cost of joint reasoning alone. The second is skill load: performance as a function of primitive counts, separated into self-load, where a skill degrades as more primitives of the same type are added, and cross-load, where it degrades as other primitive types increase. This is more informative than standard compositional benchmarks because it asks not only whether models fail at higher complexity, but why they fail.51:T511,The experiments cover 87K image-caption pairs for compositional integration analysis and 274K pairs for skill-load analysis, spanning object, attribute, and relation skills. The authors evaluate a diverse set of VLMs, including standard contrastive encoders, models explicitly trained for compositional reasoning, and non-contrastive architectures. The main findings are threefold. First, there is a consistent compositional integration cost: composed captions are harder than matched decomposed counterparts. However, this gap explains only part of the overall degradation as caption complexity increases. Second, each skill shows distinct sensitivity to primitive counts, and the degradation is not purely type-local. Models exhibit both self-load and cross-load effects, meaning that increasing relation primitives, for example, can also hurt object or attribute-related performance. Third, these patterns appear across model families, though with different magnitudes and shapes, suggesting that some architectures or training objectives may help with one bottleneck while leaving others untouched. The paper is strongest not in a single headline number, but in showing through controlled comparisons that compositional failure is a mixture of integration cost and skill-specific load effects.52:T479,TimeBraid uses a mixture-of-Transformers design with two pretrained hosts: a language model for instruction following, reasoning, and text generation, and a time-series foundation model for continuous-signal perception and zero-shot forecasting. The two are connected by interleaved global residual attention layers, which create a shared chronological context while keeping modality-specific processing intact. Inputs and outputs are represented as arbitrary sequences of segments. Each segment can be text or a univariate time series, and can be either context or target. For forecasting, the target time-series segment restates the observed history and then continues with future values, which makes forecasting fit the same interface as text generation. Training follows a two-stage curriculum: first, large-scale paired data for alignment and controllable forecasting; then task adaptation for instruction following and real-world domains. Compared with simple projection layers or signal tokenizers, the key design choice is to preserve native pretrained representations and enable cross-modal interaction through a shared attention space.53:Ta30,技术方案可以拆成四层。第一层是 Level-0 dense metric depth branch。作者采用 coarse-to-fine 的 DPT 风格解码器，融合视觉编码器的中间层特征和最终视觉 hidden states，输出全分辨率 metric depth。为了恢复绝对尺度，模型不只看 RGB，还显式输入相机内参。论文把内参编码成归一化 calibration、视场角、长宽比等紧凑描述，再通过 MLP 生成 FiLM 参数，对各尺度解码层做条件调制。这样做比把相机参数简单拼到语言 token 里更直接，因为 dense depth 分支需要的是数值尺度校准。另一个细节是高分辨率 RGB refinement pathway，用于补回空间压缩视觉 token 容易丢失的细边界、薄结构和深度突变。

第二层是 dense-to-language interface，这是全文最关键的创新。模型先基于引用框或 referring prompt 确定对象区域，再在这些区域内对预测深度和 decoder feature 做 pooling，形成 object-aligned continuous geometry tokens，并且显式绑定 object identifier。这里的设计重点不是把整张深度图塞给 LLM，而是把“哪个对象对应哪段几何证据”编码清楚，避免多对象问题里对象-数值错配。

第三层是几何信息保持机制。作者注意到，仅靠最终答案监督，geometry token 在进入语言上下文后很容易失去可恢复的 metric content。因此加入 auxiliary depth objectives，在 context interaction 前后都要求能从这些 token 中恢复对象级深度；同时加入 ranking objective，监督对象间深度顺序。这个设计很像给跨模态 bottleneck 加了信息守恒约束：不是只要求最后答对，而是要求中间表示仍然保留可读出的几何量。

第四层是 instance-level instruction tuning 与 cached continuation。模型把对象级几何 token 连同问题一起送入语言生成，但通过 cached continuation 避免对图像和问题反复编码，降低推理成本。训练任务按论文的层级划分覆盖 Level 1 的实例级测量和 Level 2 的组合推理，使模型不仅会报深度值，也会做区间筛选、相对比较、阈值判断等组合操作。

和已有工作相比，DepthLM 更偏向把深度预测吸收到语言建模里，没有显式 object-grounded evidence interface；DepthVLM 虽然也做 dense prediction 与文本联合，但这篇更强调“把模型自己的 dense metric prediction 变成对象级语言证据”，并通过前后双重监督保证数值信息在语言上下文中不被洗掉。这是它与一般 depth-aware VLM 的主要区别。54:Ta18,The method has four layers. First is the Level-0 dense metric depth branch. The model uses a coarse-to-fine DPT-style decoder that fuses intermediate vision features with the final visual hidden states to predict full-resolution metric depth. To recover absolute scale, camera intrinsics are explicitly encoded into normalized calibration, field-of-view, and aspect-ratio descriptors, then mapped through an MLP into FiLM parameters that modulate every decoder scale. This is more targeted than simply appending camera values to language tokens, because the dense branch needs direct metric calibration. A high-resolution RGB refinement pathway is added to recover thin structures, sharp boundaries, and local detail that compressed visual tokens tend to lose.

Second is the dense-to-language interface, which is the central idea of the paper. Given object boxes or referring prompts, the model pools predicted depths and decoder features over each referenced region, producing object-aligned continuous geometry tokens tied to explicit object identifiers. The point is not to feed a whole depth map into the language model, but to preserve the mapping between object references and their geometric evidence.

Third is geometry preservation. The authors argue that answer supervision alone is too weak: once geometry tokens interact with the language context, their metric content can degrade. To prevent this, they add auxiliary depth objectives that require object-level depth to remain recoverable both before and after contextualization, plus a ranking loss that supervises relative depth ordering across objects. This effectively imposes an information-preservation constraint on the multimodal bottleneck.

Fourth is instance-level instruction tuning and cached continuation. The geometry tokens are injected into answer generation together with the question, while cached continuation avoids repeatedly re-encoding the image and prompt. Training covers both instance-level measurement and compositional reasoning, so the model learns not only to estimate depth values but also to use them in interval filtering, thresholding, and relational decisions.

Compared with prior work, DepthLM absorbs depth prediction into language modeling but does not provide an explicit object-grounded evidence interface. DepthVLM jointly handles dense prediction and text, but this paper goes further in making the model’s own dense metric output the direct evidence source for object-level reasoning, with explicit supervision to keep the numeric signal intact through language interaction.55:T71e,The model size is 4B. Evaluation is organized into three levels. Level 0 measures dense metric depth prediction, where the paper reports the best average dense δ1 across nine datasets among the compared methods. This matters because the reasoning module depends on the quality of the underlying geometry. Level 1 evaluates instance-level metric depth estimation, asking whether the model can assign accurate depth to individual referenced objects. Level 2 evaluates compositional depth reasoning, where answers depend jointly on object identity, spatial relations, and numeric constraints. The paper also introduces the Depth-VQA benchmark, separating object measurement, relative reasoning, and metric-constrained reasoning. DepthEvidence achieves the highest overall reasoning accuracy on both reasoning tracks while keeping general VQA performance broadly stable relative to the base model.

The most useful part of the empirical story is the ablation logic. Camera-conditioned decoding improves metric-scale recovery. The high-resolution RGB pathway helps local structure and depth discontinuities. The dense-to-language interface is better suited than relying only on compressed visual tokens for object-level geometry binding. Geometry supervision before and after contextualization improves the recoverability of metric information from the intermediate tokens and translates into stronger Level-2 reasoning. The ranking loss helps relative-depth questions. The benchmark design is also important: many questions require both object filtering and numeric interval constraints, which makes it easier to distinguish vague spatial priors from genuine object-level metric reasoning. The paper is not just optimizing one metric; it connects dense prediction, object measurement, and final language answers in one chain.56:T562,This one is worth a close read. Start with the introduction and the Level 0/1/2 task decomposition; otherwise it is easy to misread the paper as a standard depth-aware VLM. Then focus on Figure 2 and the method section: how camera intrinsics condition the dense decoder, how the dense-to-language interface extracts object-aligned geometry tokens, and why the auxiliary depth objectives are applied both before and after language-context interaction. In the experiments, read along a three-step question: is the geometry branch accurate, is object-level metric information preserved, and does the language model actually use it for reasoning? The deeper follow-up questions are whether continuous geometry tokens generalize to 3D, video, or robotics, whether object-aligned evidence interfaces can emerge in larger native multimodal pretraining, and whether the same recoverability principle can be applied to other continuous modalities.57:T4e1,The proposed symbiotic architecture replaces the usual thin adapter with an injector. In a standard audio language model, the audio encoder produces embeddings, the adapter maps them into the LLM embedding space, and the LLM performs prefilling over the full audio sequence. Here, the injector directly writes audio-conditioned key/value tensors into the short-term memory of the LLM. Since it generates a KV cache for every LLM layer, the injector has the same number of layers as the backbone, but it can be much narrower. The injector is built from CNN-style LConv blocks rather than vanilla Transformer blocks. The rationale is that audio-to-cache conversion mostly needs local context, while the frozen Transformer backbone can handle global integration during generation. The LConv block uses depthwise 1D convolution between pointwise dense layers, with RMSNorm replacing the normalization used in Conformer-style modules for better stability under small-batch training. The described configuration uses 2048-dimensional inputs to the depthwise convolution, kernel size 15, max-pooling subsampling with stride 8, and separate affine projections into key and value spaces. RMSNorm is applied to keys, and also to values for training stability.58:T40d,LIRSeg introduces learnable latent tokens in place of explicit CoT. Training has two stages. The first stage performs supervised spatial alignment, grounding the latent tokens in object-relevant visual regions so that they encode spatial evidence rather than serving as generic placeholders. The second stage applies RL with segmentation rewards to refine these tokens under a compact token budget. Since latent tokens do not inherit the representational diversity of pretrained language tokens, the authors add three mechanisms to avoid collapse and weak exploration: extreme-advantage sampling to emphasize informative reward signals, decoupled exploration–stability updates to separate exploratory changes from representation-preserving updates, and latent diversity amplification to keep different latent tokens from converging to the same role. Compared with Seg-Zero, PixelThink, and DR2Seg, the key change is not shorter textual reasoning; it is the removal of textual reasoning in favor of visually grounded latent computation.59:T8bf,The method is built around a reverse-SFT pipeline followed by semantic-consistency RL. The system is formalized as a prompt enhancer πθ feeding a video generator Gϕ. The goal is to generate a textual condition y that is easier for Gϕ to realize faithfully. Instead of starting from a user request x and expanding it forward into a richer prompt, WanPE starts from a high-quality real video v, derives a hierarchical cinematic condition y from that video, and then reconstructs a compatible but information-sparser user request x. The pair (x, y) is used for supervised training. The motivation is straightforward: y is grounded in real video and therefore better aligned with the conditioning distribution seen by the generator, while x approximates realistic user input at inference time.

The hierarchical cinematic condition appears to be organized at the shot level rather than as a single long paragraph. It captures scene setup, entities, actions, camera language, lighting, audio or dialogue, and narrative progression across shots. This matters because cinematic planning is a coupled control problem: action, camera, pacing, editing, and atmosphere evolve together and cannot be handled well by local prompt embellishment.

After SFT, the model is optimized with SC-GRPO. The key contribution here is the reward design rather than GRPO itself. The paper defines a nine-dimensional semantic-consistency reward to check whether user requirements are preserved across the entire plan. The reward targets omissions, semantic drift, incorrect bindings between entities and attributes or actions, and temporal inconsistencies across shots. Compared with rewards based only on fluency or overall text quality, this is much closer to structured fidelity. In effect, the RL stage acts like a global verifier for long-form planning: the model is encouraged not only to sound cinematic, but to remain faithful to the original request throughout the generated plan.

Another notable point is transferability. The authors claim WanPE can transfer across video generators after format adaptation. That suggests the model is learning a more abstract planning representation rather than memorizing a single generator-specific prompt template.5a:T806,Three parts of the experimental section matter most. First is scale and headline gain. The paper trains WanPE variants from 4B to 397B on 1.05M real-world videos. According to the reported main results, WanPE-397B improves over raw prompts by up to 18.84 points for 5–15 second generation and 50.86 points for 30-second generation. The larger gain at longer duration is important: it suggests the value of prompt planning grows with temporal horizon because longer videos depend more heavily on front-end structure.

Second is the ablation evidence. Reverse construction outperforms forward rewriting, which supports the paper’s central claim that distribution alignment to real video-grounded conditions matters more than simply making prompts more descriptive. SC-GRPO improves semantic consistency by 18.6 to 23.3 points across scales. That is a substantial effect size and indicates that the main bottleneck in long-form prompt planning is requirement preservation, not surface-level wording. If the full paper breaks down reward dimensions such as omission, binding, and temporal consistency, those tables are worth reading carefully because they reveal what kinds of failures RL is actually fixing.

Third is evaluation design. The authors build WanPEval, a human-annotated benchmark covering 5 to 30 seconds and varying intent granularity, and evaluate both at the text level and through roughly 11K blind pairwise video comparisons. That is stronger than text-only evaluation because the real utility of a prompt enhancer must show up in generated video. The paper also reports that WanPE leads evaluated commercial offerings at 5–15 seconds and remains competitive with Seedance 2.5 at 30 seconds. This suggests the method is already effective in medium-duration settings, while very long generation is still partly capped by the downstream generator. If transfer experiments across generators are included in detail, those are especially useful for judging whether the model learned general planning or platform-specific prompting habits.5b:T4cc,For a quick but useful read, focus on three places. First, read the introduction carefully where the paper argues that forward rewriting and video-grounded conditioning come from different distributions. That section determines whether the work is merely a large engineering system or a genuine task reformulation. Second, inspect the method section for the exact structure of the hierarchical cinematic condition and how reverse construction builds training pairs from real videos. If that pipeline is weak, much of the gain may simply come from model scale. Third, study the SC-GRPO reward design and its ablations, especially what each of the nine reward dimensions measures and whether the training remains stable.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) comparisons among raw prompts, forward baselines, reverse-SFT, and reverse+SC-GRPO across different video lengths; (2) scaling behavior from 4B to 397B; (3) whether text-level gains match video-level blind preference; and (4) transfer across generators. A solid skim should take about 30 to 45 minutes. If only one part is worth deeper inspection, make it the reverse-construction data pipeline and the semantic-consistency reward, since those are the most reusable ideas.5c:T4dd,The method, called action forcing, starts from pixel displacement tracks across frames. Since similar egomotion directions induce recurring coherent motion patterns in the image plane, the authors run PCA over these displacement vectors and use the leading components as an egomotion basis. The first two component weights are used as low-dimensional action inputs. This avoids conditioning on dense flow or raw tracks at inference time, and it gives the action space an explicit affine structure: zero means no egomotion, scalar magnitude controls strength, sign controls direction, and axes can be combined. The world model is built by adapting a pretrained video DiT, specifically Wan2.1, under a conditional flow matching objective. The model learns a velocity field between noise latents and clean video latents, and the action is injected into the velocity network itself. This is different from applying a fixed transformation after generation; the action can shape the latent trajectory and the scene evolution. The paper also introduces an online latent egomotion critic that distills pixel-space motion into differentiable latent supervision, grounding action following without backpropagating through the video decoder or the tracker.5d:T62b,The method has three main components. First, a physical mechanism interpreter maps each action-outcome branch to a distribution over latent mechanisms rather than a point estimate. This matters because different interventions constrain the underlying physics to different degrees: a strong push may sharply identify friction, while a weak interaction may leave many mechanisms plausible. Second, the paper introduces a shared-world evidence score. Instead of forcing branch posteriors to be identical, it measures whether all branches retain common support for a shared mechanism relative to an initial-scene prior p(z|I0). The prior correction is important: it prevents uninformative branches from appearing falsely consistent simply because they remain broad and uncertain. Third, the learned compatibility signal is injected into both training and sampling. The interpreter is trained using same-world groups versus mismatched-world groups, then frozen. Its evidence score is used during flow training and also as sampling-time guidance, so the generated rollouts are nudged toward sets of futures that admit one common physical explanation. A key design choice is weak coupling: the model does not force videos or latent posteriors to collapse to the same representation, only to remain jointly explainable by one mechanism. For evaluation, the paper defines the shared-world gap: fit physical parameters separately for each branch, then fit one shared parameter set jointly across branches; the extra error under the shared fit quantifies inconsistency across interventions.5e:T454,Experiments are conducted in three controlled physical environments: Push Cube, Push Rope, and Pour Water, covering rigid-body, deformable, and particle-based dynamics. The main baseline is ACWM-DiT under the ACWM-Phys interaction setup. Relative to ACWM-DiT, OneWorld reduces the mean shared-world gap by 84.3%, which is the central result, and also improves mean M-MSE by about 7.7×10^-4, suggesting that consistency gains do not come at the expense of ordinary rollout quality. The most convincing part of the empirical section is the separation between single-branch plausibility and multi-branch physical compatibility: some baseline predictions fit physics reasonably well branch by branch, but fail badly once a single shared physical configuration is required. The paper also highlights the role of distributional mechanism inference, same-world versus mismatched-world interpreter training, and the use of the compatibility signal at both training and sampling time. The contribution is less about scale and more about closing the loop between formulation, training signal, and evaluation protocol.5f:Tac4,方法上最重要的是“串行阶段化 + 奖励硬度排序 + 难度过滤”。完整流水线是 SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF，全部基于同一个 GLM-4.5-Air-Base（106B total / 12B active）连续更新参数。

第一部分是 SFT。作者把它当成 capability-building stage，而不是格式对齐。SFT 的作用有两个：一是建立广泛能力下限，二是统一输出格式，尤其是 native <think> chat format 和多轮交互模板。这里隐含的判断是，如果 SFT 没把能力面铺开，后续 RL 只能在狭窄分布上做局部修补，容易出现 reward overfitting。

第二部分是多阶段 RL。Reasoning RL 和 Coding RL 先做，因为奖励最硬，分别依赖可验证答案或执行/测试信号，属于 RLVR。Instruction-Following RL 虽然用了 rubric-based judge，但被放在 agent 阶段之前，因为作者观察到 instruction following 离模型原有聊天能力更近，judge 可被利用的空间较小。General/Coding/Search Agent 三个阶段再把工具使用、环境交互和长轨迹决策加进来。最后才做 RLHF，用偏好型软奖励去修整开放式质量。

第三部分是 difficulty filtering。作者反复强调，训练样本要落在“可学但未掌握”的区间：已经会做的 prompt 要丢掉，大多数阶段里始终不会做的 prompt 也丢掉。这样做不是简单提纯数据，而是在 on-policy RL 中构造自动 curriculum，避免梯度浪费在零优势样本或纯噪声样本上。相比只按题目元数据分桶，这种基于当前策略表现的过滤更贴近真实学习边界。

第四部分是基础设施设计。作者明确指出，多轮 agent RL 需要 token-in/token-out rollouts，也就是把模型生成和环境返回都作为在线轨迹的一部分，而不是离线拼接。为了稳定 RL，他们使用大 batch 和 Rollout Routing Replay；后者的作用是缓解长轨迹、多环境、异步 rollout 带来的分布抖动。另一个关键点是从 SFT 到 agent 阶段保持 chat template 一致，避免模板漂移把能力变化和格式变化混在一起。对于 coding/search agent，还需要长时间稳定运行的 sandbox/service，否则 reward 噪声会直接污染策略更新。

和常见做法相比，这篇工作的区别不在单个算法，而在把“为什么先做这个、后做那个”讲得很具体。很多工作把 IF、agent、RLHF 混在一起做多目标优化；这里则明确按 reward 可验证性和被攻击风险排序。很多工作也做 hard example mining，但这里是按当前 policy 的成功带宽做动态过滤，更接近 RL 里的 learnability control。60:T927,The central design is a serial pipeline with explicit stage responsibilities, reward-hardness ordering, and difficulty filtering. The full sequence is SFT → Reasoning RL → Coding RL → Instruction-Following RL → General Agent → Coding Agent → Search Agent → RLHF, all applied to the same GLM-4.5-Air-Base checkpoint (106B total, 12B active MoE).

SFT is treated as the capability foundation. Its role is not only to align output style, but to establish broad competence and normalize the model’s interaction format, including the native <think> template and multi-turn chat behavior. The implicit claim is that if SFT does not already cover the capability surface, later RL will overfit narrow reward channels rather than build robust skills.

The RL stages are ordered by reward reliability. Reasoning RL and Coding RL come first because they rely on hard verification signals such as exact answers, execution, or tests. Instruction-Following RL uses a rubric-based judge, but it is still placed before the agent stages because instruction following is close to the model’s native chat behavior and therefore less exposed to severe reward gaming. General Agent, Coding Agent, and Search Agent then introduce tool use and environment interaction. RLHF is deliberately last, since open-ended preference rewards are the easiest to exploit.

A key mechanism is difficulty filtering. The training prompts are restricted to a productive band: prompts the current policy already solves are removed, and in most stages prompts it never solves are also removed. This turns on-policy RL into an automatic curriculum over learnable examples. Compared with static hard-example mining, the filter is policy-dependent and tracks the current learning frontier.

The infrastructure section is unusually important. The authors use token-in/token-out rollouts for multi-turn on-policy RL, large batches for stability, and Rollout Routing Replay to reduce variance and distributional jitter from long trajectories and asynchronous environments. They also emphasize strict chat-template consistency from SFT through agent stages, plus reliable sandbox services for long coding and search episodes. The paper’s novelty is less about a new optimizer or reward formula, and more about making the sequencing logic and systems constraints explicit.61:T5b0,The most useful experimental contribution is the stagewise analysis rather than the final leaderboard. The final Rufus-Air model outperforms the official GLM-4.5-Air release on every reported benchmark except Arena-Hard v2 Creative Writing, and is competitive with similarly sized open models such as INTELLECT-3 and Nemotron-3-Super. It leads on instruction-following and most alignment and agentic rows, ties Nemotron-3-Super on Terminal-Bench 2.1, trails on a few Tau2 domain rows, and is weaker on creative writing.

More importantly, each stage is evaluated against the checkpoint it starts from, not only against the final model. That design is critical in multi-stage post-training because later stages overwrite the same parameters. Without stagewise comparisons, it is hard to tell whether a gain comes from the intended stage or from accidental carryover.

The paper’s main empirical claims are that strong SFT materially raises the downstream ceiling, Reasoning RL improves not only reasoning tasks but also later instruction-following, and difficulty filtering is a major driver of stable RL gains. The excerpt already gives the practical scale: the RL stages run on 8 to 32 nodes with a 12B-active MoE model, which makes the recipe accessible outside frontier labs. When reading the full paper, the most reusable numbers are likely in the stagewise tables, the filtering ratios, and the compute table rather than the final benchmark summary.62:T432,Start with the Introduction and Recipe Overview. The four claims to anchor on are: SFT builds capability, difficulty filtering creates an automatic curriculum, stage order should follow reward reliability, and infrastructure is part of the recipe.

Then read the per-stage sections carefully, especially the data, reward, and filtering rules. The key question is not just what data they used, but why each capability is trained at that point in the pipeline rather than earlier or later. The placement of Reasoning RL before IF RL, and RLHF at the very end, deserves close attention.

Do not skip the infrastructure section. For anyone working on agent RL or long-horizon post-training, this is where much of the practical value sits: token-in/token-out rollouts, template consistency, sandbox reliability, large-batch RL, and Rollout Routing Replay.

Finally, read the benchmark and ablation tables with a stagewise lens. Focus on Figure 1, Table 1, Table 2, and Table 16. A careful read should take around 1.5 to 2.5 hours; a recipe-only pass can be done in under an hour.63:T8fc,整体框架分三层：大规模多模态 SFT 打底，IDRL 做核心后训练，PAH 做系统层外循环优化。

第一层是 SFT。Pistis-27B 和 9B 分别建立在 Qwen3.6 与 Qwen3.5 基座上。Thinking 版本用结构化 reasoning 数据做大规模多模态 SFT，Agentic 版本则进一步加入 agentic trajectories，覆盖长程规划、迭代推理、工具使用以及文本/图像混合场景。这里的作用是提供一个足够好的 cold start，因为文中明确提到 on-policy distillation 对初始 student-teacher overlap 敏感，没有合适起点时容易失败。

第二层是 IDRL。它不是把 distillation loss 和 RL loss 静态加权求和，也不是先蒸馏后 RL 的串行流程，而是在同一训练循环中交替执行 on-policy distillation 更新和 RL 更新。on-policy distillation 的对象是学生自己采样出来的序列，再用教师分布提供 token-level 密集监督；RL 则继续根据任务回报优化策略。作者的论点是：如果两种目标放在同一次更新里，会出现梯度干扰；如果完全分阶段，又失去相互校正的机会。交替更新相当于在时间上解耦目标冲突，同时保留动态互动。文中把收益归因于三点：探索更充分、策略熵保持更好、优化更稳定。

对于 agentic 长轨迹，作者再加了 PAS，step-level positive-advantage suppression。它针对的问题是 trajectory-level reward 的常见偏差：一条轨迹最后成功了，中间一些无效甚至错误的动作也可能因为共享正 advantage 而被错误强化。PAS 的做法是对这些中间步骤的正优势进行抑制，避免“搭便车式”信用分配。虽然从摘要信息看不到精确公式，但思想很清楚：不是所有位于成功轨迹上的动作都应得到正反馈。

第三层是 Pistis-Auto-Harnessing。它不改模型参数，也不改工具接口，而是用一个 Optimization Agent 基于开发集轨迹提出、验证并筛选 harness revision，例如工作流、prompt、技能调用、证据表示和路由逻辑的调整。只有在开发指标上确实变好时才保留修改，然后冻结到评测阶段。这个设计把“学策略”和“调系统”分开，减少了把系统工程收益误记到模型能力上的风险。64:Ta42,The framework has three layers: large-scale multimodal SFT for initialization, IDRL for core post-training, and PAH for system-level outer-loop optimization.

The first layer is SFT. Pistis-27B and Pistis-9B are built on Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 respectively. The Thinking variants are trained on structured multimodal reasoning data, while the Agentic variants additionally include agentic trajectories covering long-horizon planning, iterative reasoning, tool use, and mixed text-vision interaction. This stage is important because the paper explicitly notes that on-policy distillation is sensitive to student-teacher overlap and can fail without a strong cold start.

The second layer is IDRL. Instead of using a static weighted sum of distillation and RL losses, or running distillation and RL as separate stages, IDRL alternates between on-policy distillation updates and RL updates within a single training loop. In the distillation step, the student is trained against the teacher distribution on student-generated sequences, giving dense token-level supervision. In the RL step, the policy is optimized against task reward. The motivation is that a static joint loss can create objective interference within the same update, while a purely staged pipeline prevents the two signals from interacting during training. Interleaving is meant to decouple the objectives in time while still allowing them to shape the same evolving policy. The claimed benefits are better exploration, higher retained policy entropy, and more stable optimization.

For long-horizon agentic training, the paper adds PAS, or step-level positive-advantage suppression. This targets a common failure mode in trajectory-level RL: if a trajectory succeeds overall, some ineffective or even wrong intermediate actions may still receive positive credit because they share the trajectory’s positive advantage. PAS suppresses positive advantage on such steps, reducing this hitchhiking effect. The exact formula is not visible from the provided text, but the intent is clear: not every action on a successful trajectory deserves reinforcement.

The third layer is Pistis-Auto-Harnessing. PAH does not change the policy weights or the tool interface. Instead, an Optimization Agent proposes bounded revisions to the inference harness using development trajectories, validates them against a development metric, and keeps only those revisions that improve the metric. The selected harness is then frozen for evaluation. This cleanly separates model learning from workflow optimization, including prompts, skills, evidence representation, and routing logic.65:T731,The experimental story has two main tracks: Thinking models and Agentic models. For Thinking, Pistis-27B-Thinking is roughly on par with Qwen3.8-27B on 24 non-grounding benchmarks, 82.3 versus 82.4, while reaching the highest grounding average of 80.5, which is 8.6 points above Qwen3.8-27B. That is a useful result because it suggests the post-training recipe improves grounding substantially without sacrificing general reasoning. The 9B Thinking model is reported to achieve the best averages among similarly sized models on both benchmark groups.

For Agentic models, the gains over the corresponding base models are more pronounced on long-horizon interactive tasks. Relative to Qwen3.6-27B, Pistis-27B-Agentic improves BrowseComp-VL, MMSearch, VDR-testmini, and LiveVQA by 8.8, 3.3, 3.2, and 9.7 points. Relative to Qwen3.5-9B, Pistis-9B-Agentic improves the same tasks by 8.4, 8.0, 3.2, and 11.4 points. The larger gains on multimodal search and live interaction are consistent with the paper’s claim that IDRL and agentic trajectory training are especially helpful for long-horizon decision-making rather than single-turn QA.

The ablation section is likely where the paper is most informative. The authors state that IDRL outperforms pure on-policy distillation, pure RL, and a static joint objective. If the full report includes training curves, the most useful things to inspect are whether validation metrics are smoother, whether policy entropy decays more slowly, and whether the interleaving schedule matters. For PAS, the key question is whether it reduces the rate of bad intermediate actions inside successful trajectories and whether it improves sample efficiency on long-horizon tasks. For PAH, the important evidence is how much gain comes from harness optimization alone under the same environment-interaction budget.66:T4b4,A good skim should follow the order: method first, system second, results third. Start with the definition of IDRL and the training-loop diagram. The main thing to verify is the granularity of interleaving: whether it happens at the update level, batch level, or in larger alternating phases. That determines how different it really is from prior distillation-plus-RL pipelines. Then read the PAS formulation or pseudocode to see whether it is implemented through masking, clipping, or a more selective step filter. After that, inspect PAH, not just for the score gains but for how it avoids contaminating evaluation and how clearly it separates harness changes from policy learning.

In the experiments, prioritize: (1) the main ablation comparing IDRL against OPD, RL, and static joint training; (2) training stability and entropy curves; (3) consistency across 27B and 9B scales for both Thinking and Agentic variants; and (4) the standalone contribution of PAH with a fixed model. A useful skim should take about 35 to 50 minutes. If only one part deserves deeper attention, make it the IDRL interleaving mechanism and the PAS credit-assignment treatment, since those are the most transferable ideas.67:T4b6,The proposed method, GRAFT, stands for Graph-based Faithful Step-level credit assignment. It reorganizes multiple rollout trajectories from the same prompt into a trajectory graph instead of treating them as isolated chains. Nodes represent states and edges represent actions. State canonicalization merges identical or semantically similar states using exact matching or embedding-based similarity. The outgoing actions from a merged node then form an on-state action group, which is closer to the group required by the standard advantage definition. The method estimates node values by Bellman-style propagation over the graph using only terminal outcome rewards. Given these values, the step advantage is defined as A_t = gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t). The paper also introduces Graph GAE, extending generalized advantage estimation to the trajectory graph by aggregating multi-hop future advantage estimates. Compared with PRM-based approaches, GRAFT does not require step-level reward annotation. Compared with group normalization by step index, it avoids mixing different states into one baseline. Compared with resampling continuations from every intermediate state, it avoids the O(N^2 T) rollout cost.68:T430,SLCA-GRPO introduces Segment-Locked Credit Assignment. The rollout is first segmented with masks: environment tokens are excluded from policy gradients, and learnable policy tokens are split into a tool segment and a summary segment. The final contiguous learnable block is treated as the summary segment; all earlier learnable blocks, including reasoning traces and structured tool calls, form the tool segment. The method then computes separate group-relative advantages for tool-side and summary-side rewards. During optimization, tool advantages are routed only to tool tokens, and summary advantages only to summary tokens. This blocks cross-segment advantage contamination before backpropagation, without extra rollouts and without separating the agent into planner and summarizer models. Hierarchical Rewards provide segment-level feedback, and a Schema-Guided LLM Simulator supplies scalable tool-interaction rollouts. Unlike VinePPO, SPO, or GiGPO, which mainly operate along the temporal axis, SLCA operates along a structural execution-versus-articulation axis.69:T409,The paper formalizes an agent episode as a sequence of model actions and environment observations, with a binary outcome reward assigned at the end. It builds on GRPO, where multiple trajectories are sampled per task and group-relative advantages are computed from their rewards. The criticized OPSD setup conditions the same model on privileged context to obtain a stronger teacher distribution, then asks the ordinary student view to match it. This creates an irreducible information mismatch. Privileged Self-Practice changes where the privileged information is used. If the model’s rollouts on a task mostly fail, an analyzer model writes a short task-specific instruction. The system then resamples a guided group with that instruction in context. Guided and unguided groups are scored under their own sampling contexts, and advantages are computed within each group. The same GRPO objective is used; there is no loss term comparing the privileged and non-privileged views. At inference time, the extra instruction is removed.6a:T989,方法核心是 CounterRoute，一个在线 RL 框架，直接从原生支持 thinking / no-thinking 的单一 checkpoint 出发训练，不额外做该方法专用的 SFT warm-up，也不引入外部 router。形式化上，策略先对给定 prompt 采样模式 m∈{TH, NT}，再在该模式下生成回答 z。论文定义了带效率边际 b 的路由目标：只有当 thinking 的估计效用比 no-thinking 高出至少 b 时，才值得走 TH；否则优先走更便宜的 NT。这个 b 不是 token 成本的显式建模，而是 reward space 里的偏置，用来避免在两种模式质量接近时无谓思考。

训练上有两个关键设计。其一是 paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts。对一部分 prompt，强制当前策略分别在 TH 和 NT 下各生成一次回答，得到同一 prompt 下的成对反事实样本。然后比较两种模式的 utility，构造跨模式 credit。因为两条回答都来自当前策略，而不是旧策略、规则标签或外部教师，所以路由监督会随着策略能力一起更新，缓解 non-stationary target 问题。

其二是 hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment。论文采用一种“分离式 token 级赋值”规则：在最初的路由 token 上，不使用模式内 advantage，而是用经过截断或边界控制的跨模式 utility 差值来替换；在后续回答 token 上，只用该模式内部的 GRPO 优势做更新。这样路由 token 学的是“选 TH 还是 NT”，回答 token 学的是“在已选模式下怎么答得更好”，两类梯度不再混在一起。相比把整条序列统一做 policy gradient，这种做法更贴合层级决策结构。

第三个设计是 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。训练早期，为了避免初始模式偏好压制探索，模型会保留较高比例的 paired prompts，让两种模式都持续被采样并获得训练信号；随后逐步过渡到 self-routed prompts，让模型自己决定模式。这个 curriculum 的作用不是提升最终上限，而是稳定 co-learning 过程，避免一开始就被单一模式锁死。

从全文描述看，论文还强调它与 Thinkless、HGPO、TON 等方法的区别：这些方法通常先做额外的双模式 SFT 或混合微调，再用 RL 学路由；CounterRoute 则试图直接从现成 dual-mode checkpoint 出发，用在线 RL 同时学路由和两种回答策略，减少对 warm-up 数据分布的依赖。6b:T8a4,实验主体在 Qwen3-8B 和 Qwen3-14B 上进行。训练数据只用数学和合成 instruction-following prompts，但评测覆盖 9 个 held-out benchmark，包含 reasoning、coding、knowledge、commonsense 和 instruction following。主结果是：Qwen3-8B 的宏平均准确率达到 79.1%，Qwen3-14B 达到 82.4%，都优于同数据训练的 Think-Only GRPO，同时平均生成 token 更少。相对各自的 always-thinking checkpoint，CounterRoute 在 8B 上把平均生成 token 降低 51%，在 14B 上降低 41%，同时准确率还有提升。这说明它不是单纯靠少想来省算力，而是在不少简单样本上学会了直接答，并把节省下来的训练与推理预算转化成了更好的整体策略。

论文还给出一个很关键的现象：在 direct answering 本来就强的 benchmark 上，学到的 think rate 可以低到 1%，而 direct-answer 能力本身还会继续提升。这意味着 NT 分支不是被动保留，而是在 RL 中被单独训练得更强。另一个有价值的分析是 same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation：对同一个训练后的 checkpoint，分别强制 TH 和 NT 作答，再看两者性能差与模型实际学到的 think rate 是否一致。结果显示，在 held-out 的 coding、science、knowledge、commonsense 上，think rate 大体跟随“thinking 相对 direct 的经验收益”变化，尽管这些域并不在 RL 训练混合中。这说明路由策略学到的不是简单的表面模式，而是某种可迁移的价值判断。

消融主要在 Qwen3-8B 上做，重点验证四个组件：反事实成对采样、模式分离的回答优化、效率边际 b、以及 paired-to-self-routed curriculum。摘要和正文给出的结论是，这四项都对稳定训练和最终的 accuracy/token trade-off 有贡献。尤其是去掉成对反事实或去掉分离式 credit assignment 时，路由更容易被回答质量噪声污染；去掉 curriculum 时，早期模式偏好更容易自我强化，导致探索不足。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格数值，无法逐项复述所有 ablation 的具体百分点，但主结论是组件作用比较清楚，不是单一技巧堆出来的结果。6c:T8f9,CounterRoute starts from an off-the-shelf native dual-mode checkpoint, such as Qwen3, and trains everything with online RL, without method-specific SFT warm-up, routing labels, an external router, or separate models. Formally, the policy first samples a mode m in {TH, NT} for a prompt x, then generates a response z conditioned on x and m. The routing objective is defined with an efficiency margin b: thinking is preferred only if its estimated utility exceeds no-thinking by at least b; ties go to NT. This margin is a reward-space prior that biases toward the cheaper mode when quality is similar.

The first key mechanism is paired current-policy counterfactual rollouts. For selected prompts, the current policy is forced to answer once in TH and once in NT. This produces paired responses under both modes for the same prompt, allowing direct cross-mode utility comparison. Because both rollouts come from the current policy, the routing target tracks the model’s evolving capabilities instead of relying on fixed labels, heuristics, or a teacher.

The second mechanism is hierarchical counterfactual credit assignment. The paper uses a disjoint token-level rule. At the initial routing token, the usual within-mode advantage is replaced by a bounded cross-mode utility credit. For the response tokens, only within-mode GRPO advantage is used. This means the routing token learns which mode to choose, while the response tokens learn how to answer well within the chosen mode. Compared with sequence-level policy gradients over the whole output, this better matches the hierarchical structure of the decision process.

The third mechanism is a paired-to-self-routed curriculum. Early in training, the method keeps enough paired prompts so both modes continue to receive evidence and updates. Later, control is gradually transferred to autonomous self-routing. The purpose is to prevent early mode bias from collapsing exploration before the value of both modes is estimated reliably.

Relative to prior adaptive-reasoning methods such as Thinkless, HGPO, and TON, the paper’s main distinction is that it does not rely on extra dual-mode SFT or hybrid fine-tuning before RL. It tries to co-learn routing and both conditional response policies directly from a native dual-mode checkpoint.6d:T792,The main experiments use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B. RL training uses only math and synthetic instruction-following prompts, while evaluation spans nine held-out benchmarks covering reasoning, coding, knowledge, commonsense, and instruction following. The headline result is a macro-average accuracy of 79.1% for Qwen3-8B and 82.4% for Qwen3-14B. Both outperform same-data Think-Only GRPO while using fewer generated tokens on average. Relative to the corresponding always-thinking checkpoints, CounterRoute reduces mean generated tokens by 51% on 8B and 41% on 14B, while also improving accuracy.

A notable result is that on benchmarks where direct answering is already strong, the learned think rate can drop to as low as 1%, and the direct-answer branch still improves. That suggests the NT branch is not merely preserved for efficiency; it is actively trained into a stronger policy. Another important analysis is the same-checkpoint forced-mode evaluation. The trained checkpoint is evaluated once with forced TH and once with forced NT, and the empirical benefit of thinking is compared with the learned think rate. The paper reports that think rates broadly track the actual value of reasoning across held-out coding, science, knowledge, and commonsense domains, even though those domains are absent from the RL training mixture. That is a stronger sign of route-value alignment than raw benchmark averages alone.

Ablations are reported on Qwen3-8B and cover the main components: paired counterfactual rollouts, mode-separated response optimization, the efficiency margin, and the paired-to-self-routed curriculum. The qualitative conclusion is that each component matters for stability and for the final accuracy-versus-token trade-off. The provided text does not include all table values, so not every ablation delta can be quoted here, but the paper does present controlled evidence rather than relying on a single aggregate gain.6e:T516,For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, read the introduction and problem formulation to understand why routing is treated as a hierarchical decision rather than a static classifier, and how the efficiency margin b is defined. Second, read the method section around paired counterfactual rollouts and token-level credit assignment. The central idea is simple but easy to miss: routing tokens get cross-mode credit, response tokens get within-mode GRPO. Third, read the same-checkpoint forced-mode analysis, because that is where the paper shows whether routing actually tracks the value of reasoning.

If time is limited, the system overview figure, training algorithm, main results table, think-rate plots, and ablation table should be enough to grasp the contribution in about 25 to 35 minutes. For deeper reading, two questions are worth keeping in mind. One is whether this credit decomposition extends beyond binary TH/NT routing to multiple reasoning budgets. The other is whether the current reward-space efficiency margin can be replaced by a more explicit model of token cost, latency, or tool cost. A further pretraining-facing question is whether native dual-mode separability should be encouraged earlier, during pretraining or mid-training, rather than learned only at the RL stage.6f:T437,The central object is the conditional proof-difficulty function V(T|P), the difficulty of proving a target theorem T given an available premise set P. Lean 4 and mathlib provide the formal environment, and proof difficulty is operationalized through formal proof length or proof cost. Using the dependency structure in mathlib, the authors post-train a 27B model to predict V(T|P) before the proof is actually constructed. They then define intrinsic interestingness as proof length divided by statement length. The intended signal is high information density: a theorem that is short to state but hard to prove is more interesting. They also define utility as the amount by which adding a theorem to the mathematical context compresses later proofs. Utility captures reusable abstraction, while interestingness is easier to estimate locally. The paper reports a strong correlation between the two, which motivates using interestingness as a practical reward. The metric is then used both for post-training theorem generation and for inference-time pruning in recursive discovery.70:T56b,The paper first characterizes the failure of OPRD-style methods, then proposes LastOPD. In the baseline recipe, the student rolls out its own responses, the teacher scores them, and latent supervision is added by pairing student and teacher layers at matched relative depth, with a projector bridging hidden-size differences. The authors argue that this setup has two structural problems. First, depth-matched layers need not play the same functional role. Their J-Lens analysis shows that the teacher’s final answer becomes readable mainly in the last two layers, whereas the student’s answer emerges more gradually across layers. Second, common alignment metrics can be dominated by a few large dimensions, so improving similarity scores may not reflect useful functional matching. LastOPD changes the recipe in three ways. It aligns only the final hidden states immediately before the LM heads, avoiding intermediate layer pairing altogether. It uses a small trainable MLP to bridge width differences at that final interface. And it treats latent supervision as a short-lived scaffold: over the first 10 steps, the latent loss is linearly decayed while a token-level reverse top-k loss is linearly increased, after which training continues with token-only OPD. The key idea is that latent supervision is useful as an early directional signal but harmful when kept active too long.71:T595,The main setup distills Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B teachers into Qwen3-1.7B-Base using DAPO-Math-17k, with MATH-500 as the main validation benchmark. The collapse is striking. In the 4B-to-1.7B setting, latent-only OPRD raises MATH-500 from 25.4 to 46.2 within 10 steps, outperforming vanilla OPD by 28 points at that stage. But continued optimization drives the score down to 11.3, below the student’s initial level, with no recovery. The 8B teacher shows the same pattern. At the same time, the optimized alignment metric keeps improving: projected cosine similarity rises from 0.97 to 0.98 with the 4B teacher and from 0.95 to 0.98 with the 8B teacher, even as behavior deteriorates by roughly 35 points. The paper also reports that the untrained student and the 4B teacher already have mid-layer self-CKA around 0.99 despite a large capability gap on MATH-500, which further weakens the case for taking high similarity at face value. Diagnostics show that the main representational changes are concentrated in later student layers, that teacher and student have different layerwise answer-readout patterns under J-Lens, and that neither masking dominant dimensions nor remapping layers by CKA prevents collapse. On the method side, LastOPD avoids the late collapse and improves final MATH-500 over token-only OPD by 5.55 and 4.02 points in the two cross-size Qwen3 settings, while also outperforming continued joint supervision.72:T431,Read it in three passes: phenomenon, diagnosis, remedy. Start with Figure 1. It already contains the core story: early gain followed by collapse, alignment improving while behavior worsens, and mismatched layerwise readout patterns between teacher and student. Then read the analysis section to see why simple explanations do not hold up: the issue is not just insufficient training, and it is not fixed by a better layer mapping. After that, read the LastOPD method section with one question in mind: why align only the pre-head last layer, and why anneal the latent term away after just 10 steps? Finally, inspect the main results and ablations to separate the effect of alignment location from the effect of temporal crossfading. A solid skim takes about 30 minutes. The most interesting follow-ups are whether the useful latent-supervision window depends on teacher–student gap or task type, whether interpretability tools can predict which layers are safe to distill, and whether the same short-lived auxiliary-loss strategy transfers to multi-objective pretraining.73:T734,The paper builds on OPD and OPSD. In standard OPD, the student samples on-policy trajectories and an external teacher provides next-token logits at each generated prefix. The student is trained by matching these dense token-level targets. OPSD removes the external teacher by using a second copy of the same initial checkpoint as a privileged teacher. The teacher sees the problem, the ground-truth solution, and the student-generated prefix; the student only sees the problem. This transfers gold-conditioned local guidance to the student.

The limitation is that prior OPSD keeps the teacher frozen. The authors probe fixed incorrect trajectories and show that a frozen gold-conditioned teacher often prefers EOS at incorrect endpoints rather than tokens that initiate reflection or correction. Meanwhile, the student’s tendency to reflect increases during training, making the frozen teacher less suitable for later on-policy prefixes.

Dynamic Co-Evolution addresses this by updating the privileged teacher across rounds. After each training update, the resulting checkpoint initializes both the next student and a detached gold-conditioned teacher. The teacher is still frozen within a round, which preserves a stable target, but it is refreshed between rounds so that revision behaviors learned by the student can become part of the next round’s supervision. This is more adaptive than a permanently frozen teacher and more stable than a fully online teacher.

Self-Refined Concise Learning addresses the cost side of stronger revision. More self-checking and backtracking can improve correctness but also inflate output length. SRCL trains on answer-verified, shorter rewrites of the same on-policy responses. DCE improves the ability to recover from mistakes; SRCL encourages the model to keep that ability while using fewer tokens.74:T5fe,The experiments use Qwen3 models at 8B, 4B, and 1.7B scale and evaluate Average@12 on four competition-level math reasoning benchmarks. Compared with OPSD, DCE improves Average@12 by 35.41, 37.15, and 12.98 percentage points at 8B, 4B, and 1.7B respectively. Matched-budget controls indicate that the gains are not explained by longer generations alone.

SRCL is most visible under constrained inference budgets. Under the lowest tested 8K evaluation budget, DCE+SRCL reaches 35.07% Average@12 with a mean of 7,500 output tokens per response. It outperforms the OPSD test-time-scaling control by 6.60 percentage points while generating about 692 fewer tokens per response.

The teacher-behavior probes are central. On fixed incorrect Qwen3-8B trajectories from AIME 2024, AIME 2025, and AIME 2026, the frozen gold-conditioned teacher assigns 94.5% average probability to EOS at incorrect endpoints and only 22.0% to observed reflection cues such as “Wait”. After DCE, the privileged teacher’s endpoint EOS probability drops from 90.4% to 41.3%, while its probability on observed reflection tokens rises from 32.8% to 77.4%. This shows that the local supervision changes direction: from stopping at a wrong endpoint toward checking and revising.

Ablations compare per-round teacher updates with frozen, EMA, and periodic alternatives. Updating the teacher every round performs best, suggesting that teacher refresh frequency is a substantive training variable in reasoning self-distillation rather than an implementation detail.75:T445,The central concept is strategic diversity: substantive variation in how a problem is approached, not lexical variation or embedding-space distance. The paper proposes two ways to generate strategically diverse self-training data using the model itself. The first adapts Verbalized Sampling: the model lists multiple possible approaches with estimated probabilities, and each approach is then used as a hidden instruction for generating a full response. The second method, Groot, asks the model to build a hierarchical decision tree over approaches and samples distinct root-to-leaf paths. This is natural for competitive programming, where solutions branch by algorithm, data structure, and implementation choices. For story planning, where narrative decisions are interdependent and less hierarchical, the unstructured VS-style approach is more suitable. Compared with high-temperature IID sampling, both methods force the model to commit to different approaches before producing the final answer, so they change the strategy distribution rather than only perturbing token-level realization.76:T86a,实验主干基于 Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct 与 PMC-VQA。SFT 使用 10k 训练题、1.5k 验证题、2k clean test，且作者检查了训练集与 clean test 在图像内容和 image-question 对上的无重叠。三个 SFT 配置的最佳 checkpoint 都出现在半个 epoch。最关键的 clean-test 结果是：仅语言侧 LoRA 的 M1-L，correct-image accuracy 只提升 +1.10 个百分点，95% paired bootstrap CI 为 -0.85 到 +3.05，统计上并不稳；但 visual-benefit events 减少 2.40 个点，image sensitivity 下降 5.60 个点，同时样本级别上出现 155 个新获得的视觉收益案例和 203 个丢失案例。这说明净准确率几乎不变时，底层决策机制已经明显重排。作者还发现扩大适配范围到 merger 或 vision encoder 并没有带来更好的 held-out 视觉效用，反而 clean-test accuracy 更低，说明在这个数据量和任务设置下，更多视觉参数可训练并不等于更好地学会用视觉。GRPO 部分，标准 answer-only GRPO 在 2000 prompt trajectory 上持续优化，但验证集选出的 M2-500 在 clean test 上几乎不改准确率，说明 reward 在被优化，但收益没有转移到最终任务指标。证据目标部分，M3 与 M4 的差异揭示了一个重要现象：如果用 canonical option token 来计分，得到的是一种“选项支持度”信号；如果沿真实生成 token path 计分，学到的则更接近实际解码行为。作者又做了 500/1000/2000 prompt exposure 的 dose-matched 比较，发现 evidence score 的提升里既有训练暴露量带来的 acquisition，也有从训练集到验证集的 transfer，而且不同 score component 的变化方向并不一致。换句话说，看到 evidence objective 变好，不能直接推断模型更会看图，还要问是哪个 token、哪一段路径、在哪个数据子集上变好。全文的 paired transition 分析是亮点，因为它把 aggregate 指标拆回到单题层面的 gained/lost visual-benefit cases，能看清楚模型是在“把原来依赖图像的题做成了不依赖图像也能答对”，还是“真的学会了更多视觉证据”。77:T56b,The paper has three technical layers. First, it defines a controlled evaluation protocol with three conditions per question: Correct image (C), NoImage (N), and Shuffled image (S). Repairable attributes include birth date, death date, parentage, and director information. The intervention has five conditions. R0 is an unedited re-ask to verify reproducibility under greedy decoding. R1 appends the relevant fact sentence to the named rival. R2 appends a length-matched irrelevant sentence to that same rival. That makes Section 5 important: the two readouts are not interchangeable.7b:T40d,The method has three parts. First, the authors run activation patching across 25 models from 8 LLM families. This isolates the VQ bottleneck as the key architectural variable.7c:T436,The analysis builds on the view that masked diffusion models minimize kinetic energy during denoising and follow near-geodesic paths from the masked state to the output distribution. The authors interpret alignment as creating an energy barrier between safe refusal outputs and harmful compliance outputs. Known attacks then fall into two groups. PAD and DIJA obscure the safety disposition at initialization by injecting structural connectors or interleaving harmful tokens with mask spans. Anchoring attacks intervene mid-trajectory by replacing model predictions with harmful tokens at a chosen denoising step and then remasking. From this view, the paper defines three training-free logit-space detectors. The first is a step-0 ratio between refusal-token probability mass and compliance-token probability mass. The other two are trajectory-velocity signals derived with a Fisher-metric decomposition, measuring kinetic energy in complementary subspaces. The refusal and compliance token sets can be derived automatically from held-out prompts, rather than manually curated.7d:T466,The main evaluation uses LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, with additional checks on LLaDA-1.5, LLaDA-MoE-7B-A1B-Instruct, Chinese prompts, and different generation and block lengths. The datasets include 400 HarmBench behaviors, 520 AdvBench behaviors, 200 AlpacaEval instructions, and 250 XSTest safe prompts. Each model is tested under seven conditions: clean, XSTest, direct harmful prompts, PAD, anchoring at step 1, anchoring at step 8, and DIJA.
