The results show that the three signals capture different failure modes: the step-0 ratio is informative for template-style attacks, while velocity-based signals are useful for mid-trajectory interventions. In the reported stress tests, no tested attack configuration both evades all three signals and still produces harmful generations reliably. The comparison with DiffuGuard-SD is detection-focused, not a full generation-time defense comparison.7e:T78e,The proposed method, SCALPEL, is a contrastive sparse autoencoder designed to learn forget-selective features. The paper first formalizes an energy-bias view of reconstruction-based extraction. If activations decompose into multiple concept components, the marginal gain from improving reconstruction of component j scales with its energy. As a result, high-dispersion background concepts are favored over low-dispersion forget concepts. This is not presented as a full impossibility theorem, but as a useful incentive-level explanation for why standard extractors blend precise targets into broader features.

SCALPEL modifies the SAE objective with contrastive learning centered on forget anchors. Each forget example is augmented into paraphrases and rewritten variants, and different views of the same anchor are treated as positives. Negatives are sampled from retain data rather than from other forget examples. That design matters: using retain negatives helps separate target-specific structure from shared linguistic and task background, while avoiding the mistake of pushing related forget examples away from each other. After training, the SAE yields a fixed set of sparse forget-associated features. At inference time, the same feature set is available for every input, but each feature is subtracted only when activated by the encoder, producing an explicit and input-dependent internal filter.

Two details are especially important. First, the paper uses a norm-aware feature selection rule, because intervention strength depends both on encoder activation and on the magnitude of the decoder direction. Second, the theory section gives three supporting arguments: reconstruction induces energy bias, contrastive training favors target-selective sparse features, and high-scoring features admit a bound on expected background perturbation. These are best read as justification for the design, not as deletion guarantees.7f:T648,Experiments are run in the controlled TOFU author-level unlearning setting across three model families. The paper compares SCALPEL against mechanistic baselines such as PCA, NMF, and standard SAEs, as well as optimization-based unlearning methods. The evaluation is multi-axis: forgetting effectiveness, retain preservation, feature selectivity, and robustness of the removed trace.

The main empirical picture is consistent. First, at the representation-extraction level, SCALPEL learns features that are more concentrated on the forget target and less entangled with retain-side background structure than reconstruction-only methods. The paper supports this with activation analyses and feature-level diagnostics, including residual-stream studies on Qwen. Second, as an unlearning intervention, SCALPEL achieves competitive forgetting relative to optimization-based baselines while causing less collateral damage on retained knowledge. Third, the norm-aware feature ranking improves over activation-only ranking, confirming that decoder magnitude matters for practical intervention quality. Fourth, ablations show that the contrastive setup is sensitive to positive/negative construction: treating other forget examples as negatives hurts selectivity because it breaks shared target structure.

The evidence is strongest in the controlled benchmark setting. The authors are explicit that this is not certified deletion and not a full solution to GDPR-style erasure. The method removes extractable internal traces, but that does not imply all target-related information has disappeared from the parameters.80:T4de,Start with the introduction and Section 3. The energy-bias argument is the conceptual backbone of the paper; once that is clear, the SCALPEL design choices make sense. In the method section, focus on the augmentation scheme, the contrastive objective, the sparse coding setup, and the inference-time feature subtraction rule. The key design question is why negatives come from retain data rather than other forget examples. In the theory section, do not get stuck in every derivation; instead track the three main claims: why reconstruction favors background, how contrastive learning improves selectivity, and under what assumptions the background-perturbation bound holds. In experiments, read the main comparison tables first, then the ablations on norm-aware selection and contrastive sample construction.

A 30-minute skim is enough for the main method and findings. If reading more closely, the residual-stream analysis on Qwen around layer -4 is worth attention because it most directly illustrates the low-energy-target versus high-energy-background story. The main open question to keep in mind is whether this representation-level filtering remains stable on larger models, broader knowledge domains, and stronger adversarial prompting.81:T734,The method is a six-stage circuit-discovery pipeline. They start from 21 hand-written neutral prompts in single languages and define the objective around the target language probability at the first generated token. They then introduce LIHA, a head-level attribution score computed via activation patching between a clean target-language prompt and a corrupted foil-language prompt. This identifies attention heads whose activations causally push the model toward the correct response language.

Next, they run Edge Attribution Patching over source-head to destination-layer edges. EAP uses a first-order Taylor approximation to estimate the effect of replacing an upstream clean activation with its corrupted counterpart, allowing many edges to be scored with one backward pass per sample. Because this is only an approximation, they cap the candidate set at 2,000 edges per model and then run exact activation patching on each candidate edge. Only edges with sign agreement between EAP and exact patching are retained. The surviving edges are assembled into a DAG, interpreted as the verified first-token broadcasting circuit. Finally, they validate the graph with boundary ablations: removing in-graph edges should hurt language identification, while removing out-of-graph edges should not.

The structural findings are more interesting than the raw scores. Four standalone models show a recurring deep-layer hub topology, where a small number of late heads appear to broadcast language identity forward. The Pythia models also show more explicit multi-hop routing chains. By contrast, Qwen2.5-1.5B Base and Instruct fail the same necessity/irrelevance separation and also have the weakest EAP-to-exact correlation. The authors interpret this conservatively as a pipeline-reliability issue rather than evidence that Qwen lacks such circuits.82:T505,The study covers six models from four families, roughly 560M to 2.8B parameters: GPT-2, BLOOM-560M, Pythia-1B, Pythia-2.8B, and Qwen2.5-1.5B Base/Instruct. The edge search space grows with model size, from 792 scored edges in GPT-2 to 15,872 in Pythia-2.8B. For tractability, every model is truncated to a 2,000-edge candidate pool before exact verification. After sign-consistent exact patching, final graph sizes range from 816 edges for GPT-2 to 1,016 for Qwen2.5-1.5B.

The most important empirical result is not task performance but validation quality. The paper reports EAP-to-exact-patching correlations as a sanity check on the attribution stage. The four standalone models show stronger agreement and cleaner boundary-ablation behavior, which makes their extracted graphs more credible as functional circuits. The Qwen pair shows weaker correlation and weaker necessity/irrelevance separation, so those graphs should be treated with caution. Another useful aspect is that the analysis goes beyond listing important heads: it verifies head-to-layer edges, which is closer to a causal routing account.

That said, the dataset is tiny, only 21 prompts, so the claims should be read as a careful case study rather than a broad statistical statement about multilingual pretraining.83:T597,The framework is built on finite structural causal models. The evaluator has access to the full state ξ=(X,H), while the learner may not observe the latent context H. For a query z=(ξ,a), the evaluator defines a structural index σ_M(ξ,a), which records the active context class, the directly affected variable, the value class, and the first structural response delay. A mechanism memory μ is a finite set of tuples θ=(a,c,y,v,δ), and the answer map T_μ(z) is evaluated against the ground-truth mechanism map. The exact mechanism risk R_Q measures full answer equivalence under a fixed probe distribution Q; coordinate risks decompose errors over context, target, value, and delay, while missed and spurious mechanism risks give operational diagnostics. The main theoretical result expresses optimal probe error as a Bayes decision risk and shows that zero error is possible exactly when each learning-interface fiber lies inside a single probe-answer fiber. The adaptation setup introduces a schema map φ from source to target memory, stable and shifted index sets, and losses L_stab and L_shift. Pure transfer fails on shifted mechanisms, while broad relearning can corrupt stable ones. The proposed Causal Core mechanism uses evidence-gated writing and filtered readout, with gates estimated from paired action/reference interventions or propensity-corrected observational data under standard identification conditions.84:T490,The model abstraction starts with an unobserved physical state x, an observation o=h(x), a fixed language instruction, and an internal representation λ(x) produced by the VLA backbone. A stochastic policy π then generates a continuous-time open-loop action chunk u(t), which is treated as the control input to a nonlinear control-affine dynamical system. Quantities of interest are defined along the controlled trajectory rather than as static labels. For probing, the work constructs an ideal representation in which multiple physical quantities and their propagated values under candidate action trajectories admit shared linear readouts. For steering, it introduces a path-signature-based exponential-family policy. Path signatures summarize continuous action paths through iterated-integral features, and the exponential-family geometry yields a dually flat statistical manifold. This provides a formal link between linear probes in representation space and linear steering of action-trajectory distributions. The key difference from standard LLM LRH is that the represented direction is tied to future dynamics and policy geometry, not only to a static concept.85:T428,The authors define a growing heterogeneous manifold-mixture model where the number of components, weights, reach, separation, and perturbation scales may change with sample size. Each component can have its own intrinsic dimension and smoothness. They first prove an aggregate minimax lower bound, denoted R_n, which accounts for each component’s difficulty through dimension, smoothness, and effective sample size. They then construct an oracle tangent local-polynomial estimator: it estimates local charts and tangent coordinates, and performs reduced-dimensional polynomial regression in those coordinates. The oracle supplies dimension, smoothness, and bandwidth, but not the tangent projector or the task function. A structure-informed transformer is then built using softmax attention and ReLU feed-forward networks to implement geometric preconditioning, chartwise selection, and local reduced regression in one forward pass. The final analysis separates near-ERM risk into in-context error, approximation error, finite-task error, and optimization error.86:T9b7,技术路线可以拆成“人类提供什么”和“agent 决定什么”两部分。

人类提供的是 Research Skills。它们不是逐实验的人工指令，而是把专家经验编码成可执行的操作模板、代码资产、权限边界和流程约束。论文强调 high-density prior, low-frequency intervention：人类把成熟做法一次性写成可复用技能，之后不再频繁介入具体实验决策。这样做的目的，是把经验保留在系统里，但把搜索权交给 agent，而不是让 agent 在完全无先验的空间里盲搜。

agent 端由 Codex GPT-5.6-Sol（xhigh reasoning）承担。它从 base checkpoint 和可用算力出发，先构建 executable task pool，再基于 verified capability-gap trajectories 对 Qwen3.6-27B 做 cold-start。随后训练流程不是直接从 SFT 跳到 RL，而是先经过 OPSD，再过渡到 RLVR。根据正文描述，OPSD 阶段里至少发生了三类关键调整：其一，evaluation 会反过来决定哪些数据进入训练，说明数据池不是静态的，而是被在线证据筛选；其二，受控消融改变了 self-teacher 可见的证据范围，作者借此诊断 teacher 何时在利用泄漏信息、何时在学真实能力；其三，原有目标函数出现 collapsing objective，迫使 agent 把学习规则改成 verifier-anchored credit，也就是让 credit assignment 更紧贴可验证结果，而不是依赖容易漂移的代理信号。

RLVR 阶段则处理另一组问题：reward exploits、false verdicts、length-dependent degeneration。对应的修补方向分别是重写 reward eligibility、调整优化过程、控制 trajectory budgeting。这里最值得注意的是，论文没有把 RLVR 写成一个固定 recipe，而是把它描述成一系列失败后的重设计：奖励被利用，就收紧资格；verifier 有误判，就修改奖励语义或过滤机制；长输出导致退化，就把预算和优化目标一起改。这个叙述方式很像真实工业训练，而不是干净的学术设定。

从模型定位看，iCoder-27B 是一个面向工业编码的专门模型，任务覆盖 RTL 设计和 GPU kernel 优化。选择这两个方向有明确原因：它们都能用可执行 verifier 检查正确性，同时又要求性能意识和系统约束，不是普通代码补全就能解决。论文因此把“可验证环境中的 agent-led model development”落在一个反馈足够硬、但搜索空间仍然很大的场景里。87:T749,结果部分最醒目的是 iCoder-27B 在多个工业代码基准上的竞争力。相对同尺寸的 Qwen3.6-27B，iCoder 在 RTLLM 上从 49.6 提升到 68.0，增幅 18.4 分；在 VerilogEval Spec-to-RTL 上从 70.1 提升到 86.3，增幅 16.2 分；在 KernelBench L2 correctness 上从 28 提升到 74，约 2.64 倍。这个幅度说明它不是小修小补，而是任务能力被显著重塑。

与更大模型相比，iCoder 也有竞争力。论文给出的数字是：在 RTLLM 上超过 DeepSeek-V4-Pro（68.0 vs. 67.5）；在 KernelBench L1 correctness 上接近翻倍于 DeepSeek-V4-Pro（61 vs. 32）。对闭源前沿模型，iCoder 在 RTLLM 上高于 GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 4.8、Gemini 3.5 Flash（68.0 vs. 66.0/64.7/63.5）；在 KernelBench L1 上也高于 GPT-5.5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash，并超过 Claude 的 55 达到 61。TritonBench-G 上它与 Claude Opus 4.8 持平在 20.1，高于 GPT-5.5 的 19.5 和 Gemini 3.5 Flash 的 14.9。

论文还给了更贴近使用场景的 case study。对 8 个 RTL design 任务，iCoder 距 HY3 和 DeepSeek-V4-Pro 分别只差 1.1 和 4.5 分，但使用的输出 token 仅为它们报告值的 51% 和 33%。这说明它不仅正确率高，推理开销也更省。对选取的 8 个 GPU operator，它在其中 2 个上达到 strongest archived endpoint，说明其优化能力不只是 benchmark 分数上的偶然。

从全文表述看，实验的另一条主线是开发过程中的 ablation 和失败分析，而不仅是最终榜单。作者强调 evaluation 改变训练数据进入条件、controlled ablation 改变 self-teacher 证据、objective collapse 触发学习规则重写、reward exploit 和 false verdict 改写 RLVR 设计。这些内容如果正文给出具体表格和时间线，会比最终分数更值得看，因为它们揭示了 agent 是如何做研发决策的。88:Ta30,The setup is organized around a division of labor. Humans provide Research Skills: reusable, executable operational procedures, code assets, permission boundaries, and process scaffolds distilled from expert model-development practice. The paper frames this as high-density prior, low-frequency intervention. The point is not to remove human expertise, but to compress it into reusable machinery so that the agent can search over concrete development decisions without requiring constant human steering.

The agent is Codex GPT-5.6-Sol running at high reasoning effort. Starting from a base checkpoint and available compute, it first builds an executable task pool, then cold-starts Qwen3.6-27B on verified capability-gap trajectories. Training does not jump directly from supervised initialization to RL. Instead, the pipeline goes through OPSD and then RLVR.

The OPSD stage appears to be where much of the development logic happens. The paper highlights at least three important dynamics. First, evaluation changes which data are admitted into training, so the data mixture is not static but filtered by ongoing evidence. Second, controlled ablations alter what evidence the self-teacher can access, which is a way to diagnose when the teacher is exploiting leakage versus learning transferable capability. Third, the original objective collapses, forcing the agent to redesign the learning rule around verifier-anchored credit. That means credit assignment is tied more tightly to executable verification rather than to softer proxy signals that drift or become exploitable.

The RLVR stage addresses a different set of failures: reward exploits, false verdicts, and length-dependent degeneration. The corresponding fixes involve changing reward eligibility, modifying optimization behavior, and redesigning trajectory budgeting. One of the strongest aspects of the paper is that RLVR is not presented as a fixed recipe. It is presented as a sequence of failures and revisions: when reward is exploited, tighten eligibility; when the verifier is wrong, revise reward semantics or filtering; when long outputs degrade behavior, adjust both budget and optimization. That is much closer to real model development than a static benchmark loop.

The task domain is industrial coding, specifically RTL design and GPU kernel optimization. That choice is sensible. Both domains offer executable verification, but they also require exact reasoning, systems awareness, and performance-sensitive optimization. This gives the agent a hard feedback signal without collapsing the problem into ordinary code completion.89:T760,The headline results are strong for a 27B model. Relative to the same-size Qwen3.6-27B, iCoder improves RTLLM from 49.6 to 68.0, a gain of 18.4 points. On VerilogEval Spec-to-RTL it improves from 70.1 to 86.3, a gain of 16.2 points. On KernelBench L2 correctness it rises from 28 to 74, about 2.64x. Those are large deltas, suggesting substantial task-specific capability reshaping rather than marginal tuning.

The model is also competitive against much larger systems. The paper reports that iCoder slightly exceeds DeepSeek-V4-Pro on RTLLM (68.0 vs. 67.5) and nearly doubles its KernelBench L1 correctness (61 vs. 32). Against proprietary frontier systems, iCoder beats GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.5 Flash on RTLLM (68.0 vs. 66.0 / 64.7 / 63.5). On KernelBench L1, it also exceeds GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash and surpasses Claude’s 55 with 61. On TritonBench-G, it matches Claude Opus 4.8 at 20.1 while outperforming GPT-5.5 at 19.5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash at 14.9.

The case studies are also informative. On eight RTL design tasks, iCoder comes within 1.1 and 4.5 points of HY3 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro while using only 51% and 33% of their reported output tokens. That suggests better efficiency, not just better correctness. On selected GPU operators, it reaches the strongest archived endpoint on two of eight cases, indicating that the optimization ability is not purely benchmark-specific.

Equally important is the process evidence described in the paper. Evaluation changes data admission, controlled ablations change self-teacher evidence, objective collapse triggers a redesign of the learning rule, and reward exploits plus false verdicts force RLVR changes. If the full paper includes tables or timelines for these transitions, those are likely more informative than the final leaderboard numbers because they reveal how the agent actually made development decisions.8a:T574,A good first pass has three steps. Start with the introduction to pin down the actual claim: not fully closed-loop self-improvement, but agent-led development under a one-time injection of executable human expertise. Then read the section on Human Prior: Executable Research Skills carefully. The key question is what exactly these skills contain: SOPs, code templates, permission boundaries, experiment harnesses, or stronger hand-authored recipes. That determines how to interpret the level of autonomy. Third, read the training pipeline sections with attention to the transitions between cold-start, OPSD, and RLVR, and to the failures that trigger each recipe revision. If the paper includes a development timeline, experiment tree, dataflow diagram, or reward-redesign table, prioritize those.

A 35 to 50 minute skim should be enough to capture the main story. If you only care about model quality, the main results table is sufficient. But the real value is in the process details: how evaluation feeds back into data selection, why the objective collapses, how verifier-anchored credit is defined, how reward eligibility is tightened, and how length-dependent degeneration is diagnosed and mitigated. The right reading stance is cautious: this is agent-led development under strong human priors and institutional scaffolding, not fully autonomous research without hand-designed structure.8b:T907,方法上有四个部分。第一是 Extractor 数据集本身。作者选择一个真实而且不算简单的逆向工程工具作为开发对象：从 Apple Objective-C / Mach-O 二进制中恢复 protobuf descriptor。整个项目 21,000 行生产代码，测试规模相当，210 个 commits，25 个 sessions，678 条用户指令，全部由 Claude 模型生成，没有人工编写代码、测试或 commit。这个设置的价值在于，它不是 toy repo，也不是只截取若干聊天片段，而是完整保留了开发过程。

第二是代码 provenance tracing 工具。作者提出两种追踪方法。其一是基于 control-flow-graph block decomposition 加 git log -L 历史追踪，并处理 rename bridge，用来把代码块级别的变更追溯到具体来源事件。这里的来源不只是用户指令，也包括 AI 的自发发现和自我修正。其二是 session transcript mining，从工具调用日志中恢复那些在 session 内已经被修正、因此不会出现在 commit 历史里的代码生成错误。这个点很关键，因为只看 git history 会低估模型犯错率，尤其低估“先写错、再自救”的频率。

第三是三套 taxonomy。用户指令 taxonomy 扩展了 Tang 等人的 IDE-chat 分类，使其适用于多轮 CLI coding agent 场景，并新增 cross-session coordination 与 correction of AI conduct 两类。commit provenance taxonomy 则把传统软件工程里的 Perfective / Corrective / Adaptive maintenance 进一步拆开，区分“为什么改”和“怎么发现要改”。response reliability taxonomy 是这篇文章最有新意的部分之一：作者不只看代码结果，而是把 AI 对用户的陈述按 reporting / verification、mechanism explanation、root-cause diagnosis、design fix proposal 等类型分类，再用软件工件去核验这些陈述是否准确。

第四是基于上述工具和 taxonomy 的过程分析。作者把开发过程区分为 proactive 与 reactive 两类触发机制，前者是主动扩展、规划、实现，后者是对 bug、测试失败、异常现象的响应。这样做的目的，是理解 AI coding agent 到底是在“持续前进，偶尔修错”，还是“频繁出错，被动补洞”。全文结论偏向前者，但同时指出中间错误并不少。8c:T9c8,The work has four technical components. First is the Extractor dataset itself. The target project is a real reverse-engineering tool that recovers protobuf descriptors from Apple Objective-C / Mach-O binaries. It is not a toy repository. The project contains 21,000 lines of production Python code, a similarly sized test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 user instructions. All code, tests, and commits were authored by Claude models, with no human-written code. The value of this setup is completeness: it preserves the full development process rather than a thin slice of it.

Second are two provenance-tracing tools. One combines control-flow-graph block decomposition with git log -L history tracing, including rename bridging, to map code changes back to specific source events. Those events include user instructions, autonomous discoveries, and self-corrections. The other mines session transcripts and tool-use logs to recover code-generation errors that were fixed within a session and therefore never appear in commit history. This is a key methodological point. Commit-only analysis systematically underestimates how often the model first writes something wrong and then repairs it.

Third are three taxonomies. The instruction-intent taxonomy extends Tang et al.’s IDE-chat taxonomy to multi-turn CLI coding-agent interaction and adds categories such as cross-session coordination and correction of the AI’s own conduct. The commit-provenance taxonomy extends the standard Perfective/Corrective/Adaptive maintenance framing by separating why a change was needed from how that need was discovered. The response-reliability taxonomy is one of the more original parts of the paper. Instead of only checking code outcomes, the authors classify the agent’s user-facing claims into categories such as fact reporting, mechanism explanation, root-cause diagnosis, and design-fix proposal, then verify those claims against the software artifacts.

Fourth is the process analysis built on top of these tools. The authors distinguish proactive development from reactive development. Proactive work means planning, extending, and implementing ahead of failures. Reactive work means responding to bugs, failed tests, or observed problems. This framing helps answer whether the agent mostly advances the project and occasionally repairs mistakes, or whether it is mainly patching its own failures. The paper finds more of the former, but with a nontrivial amount of hidden intermediate error.8d:T716,The key results come from full-process annotation rather than final-repo statistics. On scale, the project contains 21k lines of production code, a roughly comparable test suite, 210 commits, 25 sessions, and 678 cleaned user instructions. On interaction patterns, CLI-based coding-agent instructions differ from prior IDE-chat datasets by putting more weight on comprehension, planning, and consultation rather than one-shot code requests. On development dynamics, 86–90% of commits and 89–90% of code blocks trace back to proactive triggers rather than reactive responses to bugs or failed tests. In this case study, development is mostly forward-moving rather than purely error-driven.

The most informative numbers are about hidden errors and conversational reliability. By mining transcripts rather than only commits, the authors estimate that 14.3% of AI code-generation events contain a real error that is later caught by the AI-authored test suite before any commit is made. Standard commit-based analysis would miss these errors entirely. For user-facing responses, Claude is relatively reliable when reporting or verifying facts at 94.3% accuracy, somewhat worse when explaining an existing mechanism at 91.1%, lower again for root-cause diagnosis at 89.3%, and substantially weaker when proposing a design fix at 79.4%. Overall, roughly one in four to five interactive responses contains at least one inaccuracy. That result is important because it shows that code generation ability and explanation reliability are related but not interchangeable.

The empirical strength of the paper is not breadth across many repositories. It is traceability. The authors recover intermediate mistakes, temporary hypotheses, and corrected misconceptions that are usually erased from the visible software history.8e:Tadc,方法由两部分组成：IterSynth 范式本身，以及配套的 Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization（RDPO）。

先看 IterSynth。它把一次 deep search 拆成 Planner 和 Synthesizer 两个交替角色，但这两个角色不是两套模型，而是同一个 LLM 在不同 role prompt/格式下的两种行为模式。Planner 只看压缩后的 summary state，负责判断还缺什么信息、下一步该搜什么、何时继续探索。Synthesizer 读取新检索到的证据，对 summary 做增量更新：吸收有用事实、处理冲突、丢弃噪声、维护当前结论和未解决问题。这样，summary 不再是外部 memory module 的被动压缩结果，而是 agent policy 的显式输出和持久状态。

这个设计同时解决两个问题。对 role coupling，它通过角色分工降低单步决策的能力混杂度。Planner 不需要在长证据块里写最终答案，Synthesizer 也不需要决定全局搜索策略。对 context accumulation，它不再把完整历史一直塞回上下文，而是让 summary 成为受控、紧凑、可更新的状态表示。相比多 agent 系统，它不需要多模型协作和额外部署复杂度；相比已有 summary-based agent，它把摘要更新纳入训练目标，而不是把 summarization 当外接工具。

再看训练。作者采用 SFT → RL 的两阶段 recipe。SFT 的作用是教会模型 Planner–Synthesizer 协议、角色切换格式和基本迭代搜索行为，但作者明确指出 imitation 只能学会“怎么按这个协议行动”，不能充分优化“什么时候搜、搜什么、保留什么证据、两个角色如何协同”。因此引入 RDPO。

RDPO 的关键不是简单加一个中间奖励，而是按角色做 credit assignment。它把终局 outcome reward 和 turn-level rubric evaluation 结合起来，再分别为 Planner 和 Synthesizer 计算 group-relative advantages。这样做的动机很直接：Planner 的好坏更多体现在 query 是否有信息增益、是否识别到知识缺口、是否避免冗余搜索；Synthesizer 的好坏则体现在证据整合、冲突处理和 summary 更新质量。如果沿用普通 GRPO 或 outcome-only RL，两个角色共享一条回报，梯度会把不同错误来源混在一起，尤其在长轨迹里更严重。RDPO 通过 role-specific advantage 让更新方向更贴近各自职责。

从范式上看，这篇工作和 ReAct 的差异不只是“多了摘要”，而是把搜索过程从线性 action history 改成了围绕 summary state 的迭代闭环。和外部 summarizer 方法相比，它避免了摘要器与主 policy 目标不一致的问题。和多 agent 方法相比，它保留单参数集部署优势，同时通过角色解耦获得部分 specialization 收益。8f:T9f2,The method has two parts: the IterSynth search paradigm and the associated Role-Decoupled Policy Optimization (RDPO) training objective.

IterSynth alternates between two roles, Planner and Synthesizer, instantiated by the same LLM rather than by separate models. The Planner reads only the compact summary state and decides what information is still missing, what to search next, and whether exploration should continue. The Synthesizer reads newly retrieved evidence and updates the persistent summary by integrating useful facts, resolving conflicts, filtering noise, and maintaining the current state of knowledge. In this design, the summary is not an external memory artifact. It is the explicit, learned state of the search process.

This addresses both target problems. Role coupling is reduced because planning and evidence integration are no longer forced into the same local decision. Context accumulation is reduced because the agent no longer carries the full search history forward; it carries a controlled, compact, updateable state instead. Compared with multi-agent systems, this avoids extra models and coordination overhead. Compared with prior summary-based agents, it makes summary updating part of the policy itself rather than an auxiliary external module.

Training follows an SFT-to-RL recipe. SFT teaches the Planner–Synthesizer protocol, role formatting, and basic iterative search behavior. But the authors explicitly note that imitation mainly teaches the interaction pattern, not the deeper decisions of when to search, what evidence to preserve, or how the two roles should coordinate. That is why they introduce RDPO.

RDPO combines terminal outcome rewards with turn-level rubric evaluations and computes group-relative advantages separately for Planner and Synthesizer actions. The motivation is straightforward: the Planner should be rewarded for identifying information gaps, issuing informative queries, and avoiding redundant exploration, while the Synthesizer should be rewarded for evidence integration, conflict handling, and summary quality. Standard outcome-only GRPO mixes these error sources together, which is especially harmful in long trajectories. Role-specific advantages make the gradient signal better aligned with each role’s responsibility.

Conceptually, the difference from ReAct is not just the addition of summaries. IterSynth changes the search loop from a linear action history into an iterative process centered on an explicit summary state. That is the main modeling contribution.90:T60c,The headline result is that IterSynth-8B reaches 50.7% average performance across five long-horizon deep-search benchmarks: GAIA-text-only, xBench-2505, xBench-2510, BrowseComp, and BrowseComp-ZH. This is 4.2 points above the strongest prior agent at 8B or below, while remaining competitive with several 30B-scale agents at less than one third of the parameter budget.

The training ablations are particularly informative. The SFT baseline scores 44.1%. Outcome-only GRPO raises this to 48.9%. RDPO further improves it to 50.7%. So RL itself contributes a large gain, and role-decoupled credit assignment adds another 1.8 points on top. The paper notes that this extra gain is strongest on exploration-heavy benchmarks, which suggests that RDPO improves search behavior rather than only answer polishing.

A key diagnostic appears in Appendix H: even with a 64K context window, more than 59% of ReAct trajectories on BrowseComp fail to terminate before context exhaustion. This directly supports the paper’s claim that the bottleneck is not simply context length, but the way search state is represented and updated.

The prompting-transfer results are also useful. IterSynth is not only a trainable 8B-agent recipe; it also works as a prompting paradigm for frontier models such as Claude-4.5-Opus and DeepSeek-V3.1, consistently outperforming ReAct and IterResearch, with gains of up to 10 points over ReAct on BrowseComp-ZH. That suggests the paradigm captures a generally better search organization rather than a narrow model-specific trick.91:T42b,Start with the Introduction and Figure 1. The paper clearly contrasts three paradigms: multi-agent decomposition, external summarization, and IterSynth. Once that structural difference is clear, the rest of the method becomes much easier to follow.

Then read the methodology in two passes. First, focus on what each role sees and produces, and how the summary state is updated. Second, study RDPO carefully, especially why advantages are computed separately by role instead of using a single GRPO-style return for the whole trajectory. If you have worked on agent RL before, this is the part where the paper’s real contribution becomes obvious.

In the experiments, prioritize the main benchmark table, the ablations, and Appendix H. The main table answers whether the method works, the ablations explain why, and Appendix H shows where ReAct actually breaks. If time is limited, read the average benchmark results, the SFT → GRPO → RDPO progression, and the prompting-transfer section. A quick pass takes under an hour; a careful read takes around 90 minutes.92:T412,TRACER uses a two-stage training recipe. First, supervised fine-tuning on real user dialogues teaches the model to generate user responses and to emit structured annotations: a rationale and an ordinal intent score. The intent score acts as an interpretable proxy for the user’s evolving commitment or engagement state. Second, the simulator is trained with multi-turn reinforcement learning while interacting with a fixed assistant. Rewards combine terminal outcome agreement and trajectory alignment against paired human logs. Dynamic time warping is used to align trajectories with different lengths and conversational pacing. A deviation-aware advantage modulation mechanism then uses local alignment errors, accumulated over discounted trajectory suffixes, to scale turn-level policy updates while preserving the direction of the session-level advantage. Compared with static persona prompting, the method optimizes state evolution; compared with standard turn-level optimization, it assigns credit using the whole dialogue trajectory.93:T4a1,TalkMesh places agents on a sparse communication graph. Each agent uses a frozen base model M with two LoRA adapters: a confidence head V and a talk policy T. Inference has five stages. First, agents independently sample proposals, matching the independence assumption of self-consistency. Second, V scores each proposal using the sigmoid of the Yes-versus-No logit gap under a fixed verification prompt. Third, the highest-confidence agent becomes the speaker and emits a hint capped at 112 tokens. Fourth, listeners whose confidence is below 0.5, or who did not produce an answer, revise their proposals using the hint. A revision is accepted only if V scores it higher than the original. Fifth, agents run gossip consensus to approximate a centralized confidence-weighted vote without a coordinator. The confidence head is trained as an outcome verifier. The talk policy is trained inside the protocol with GRPO using a flip reward: +1 when a revision changes a wrong answer to a correct one, and -1 for the reverse. The speaker receives the mean flip reward over its listeners. Training uses a curriculum over rollout size K = 3, 5, and 8, while evaluation scales to larger meshes.94:T402,The main experiments compare self-consistency, confidence reranking without messages, and the trained mesh. With three agents, the trained mesh reaches the accuracy of self-consistency with 32 samples. At N = 32, SmolLM3-3B on MATH-500 improves from 0.492 under self-consistency to 0.722 with TalkMesh, while reranking without messages reaches 0.590. Qwen3.5-0.8B on GSM8K improves from 0.568 to 0.705, with reranking at 0.655. In an attack setting with N = 8 and four compromised agents submitting the same wrong answer with claimed confidence 0.99, majority vote drops to 0.000 on 150 test problems. The defended mesh, which rescores solutions and gates revisions, retains 0.507 on Qwen3.5-0.8B GSM8K versus 0.667 without attack; an undefended version drops to at most 0.007. Additional evaluations cover SwarmBench and traffic control. On the severe traffic subset, messages reduce person delay for Qwen3.5-0.8B, 2B, and 4B meshes by 23.6±6.7 seconds; over all 70 scenarios, the 4B mesh reduces delay by 11.4±6.9 seconds.95:T423,The starting point is Karpathy’s AutoResearch loop: an LLM edits training code, launches an experiment, and keeps changes that improve a held-out metric. The authors deploy this pattern in two production representation-learning systems at Amazon and identify five recurring failure modes: infrastructure fragility, agent memory decay, search-direction stagnation, iteration-cost asymmetry, and metric fixation. The proposed scaffolding follows three principles. Prevent uses a semantic gate before execution, which is worthwhile when a failed run wastes many GPU-hours. Persist stores durable cross-job memory, so the agent does not repeat known mistakes or forget prior findings during multi-week campaigns. Redirect triggers strategic reframing when local code or hyperparameter edits stop producing progress. The implementation is a three-agent extension of AutoResearch. The main design lesson is cost dependence: expensive iterations justify heavier pre-run checks, while cheaper iterations can rely more on post-run revert and lightweight supervision.96:T70a,The paper analyzes discrete heavy-ball momentum dynamics in a river-valley model of the loss landscape. The geometry is decomposed into a low-loss, low-curvature, slowly bending river manifold and sharp orthogonal valley directions. The optimization challenge is not merely to descend, but to move quickly along the river without letting oscillations in the sharp directions destabilize the trajectory.

The main result is that momentum enlarges the largest tolerable learning rate by a leading factor of roughly (1+β)/(1-β) relative to vanilla GD. This factor is classical for quadratic objectives, but the nontrivial part here is showing that it still governs the leading stability threshold in a non-convex setting where the river and valley subspaces rotate and interact over time. Because of that rotation, gradient and momentum components leak across subspaces, so one cannot reuse a fixed-eigenspace argument.

To handle this, the authors develop a new inductive analysis that tracks both gradient and momentum projections onto river and valley directions, while controlling their mutual interference across iterations. A second key conclusion is interpretive: for a flat and slowly spinning river, momentum itself does not substantially change the intrinsic speed along the river. The acceleration mainly comes from enabling a much larger stable learning rate. In that sense, momentum acts more as a stabilizer that permits aggressive step sizes than as a direct source of extra river-direction acceleration.

The paper also improves the largest tolerable learning-rate bound for vanilla GD in the same river-valley framework. That side result suggests the proof machinery is not narrowly tailored to momentum alone, but strengthens the analytical understanding of the landscape model itself.97:T5fb,From the available full-text content, this is primarily a theory paper, with experiments serving to validate the mechanism rather than to establish a new large-scale training recipe. The empirical phenomenon tied to the theory is clear: under WSD-like schedules, a long high-LR phase can produce higher observed loss than cosine scheduling because of oscillations across sharp valley walls, while still making faster progress along the river. Once the learning rate is sharply decayed, those oscillations are suppressed and the hidden progress becomes visible as a lower final loss.

The paper also mentions synthetic river-valley loss constructions for visualization and connects its analysis to prior probing of LLM pretraining landscapes in Wen et al. (2025). The most important empirical checks are therefore: (1) momentum remains stable at larger learning rates on synthetic river-valley landscapes; (2) the predicted stability-threshold enlargement matches the observed stable region; and (3) the seemingly paradoxical pattern of higher intermediate loss but better final optimization can be explained by separating river progress from valley oscillation.

The provided text does not include full tables, model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact improvement numbers, so those should not be invented. When reading the original, the most useful experimental artifacts to extract are the stability-boundary plots, the comparisons against vanilla GD, and any quantitative alignment between the theorem and observed training dynamics.98:T58c,Read it in the order of phenomenon, model, theorem, then proof technique.

Start with the introduction and lock onto the practical question: why can a long high-LR phase plus sharp decay outperform smoother schedules, and what role does momentum play there? Then jump to Theorem 4.1. That is the central statement of the paper: the maximum stable learning rate is enlarged by about (1+β)/(1-β).

After that, spend time on Lemma 5.1 and the surrounding proof structure. This is where the real novelty sits. The important part is not only the final factor, but how the authors control dynamics when the river and valley subspaces rotate and when gradient and momentum components interfere with each other. While reading, focus on three things: how the river/valley projections are defined and updated, what assumptions encode “flat” and “slow-spinning,” and how the error terms are prevented from accumulating into instability.

If time is limited, read the theorem statements, proof sketches, and the main figures first, then return to the technical induction details. Also check the remark on the improved vanilla-GD learning-rate bound; it helps assess whether the analytical framework has broader value beyond the momentum case.

A careful read will likely take 1.5 to 2.5 hours. Unlike masked diffusion, UDM corruption replaces tokens with ordinary vocabulary tokens, so the model cannot directly tell whether an observed token is clean or noise. Diffusion time can therefore encode how much the observed context should be trusted. The work explains why the population-optimal UDM predictor is time-dependent, while time-agnostic predictors can still work well in language-scale finite-data settings.","importance":"The result is useful for diffusion LM design. This helps explain why time-agnostic predictors are natural for masked diffusion and can remain competitive for UDMs, even though UDMs do not reveal corrupted positions. For pretraining, the broader lesson is that an input variable may be theoretically informative but weakly used when the empirical data distribution is sparse and training sequences are well separated.","technical_approach":"$21","experiments":"The empirical analysis measures how much trained language UDMs use time. The predictive gain from explicit time conditioning is similarly concentrated near high noise. workload、硬件和质量口径下评估。","experiments":"论文给出的关键数字很有用。Llama-3-70B 在 BF16 下权重约 140 GB，已经超过单张 80 GB HBM 加速卡容量。其 KV cache 公式为 Bkv = 2·L·nkv·dh·wkv·s。对 Llama-3-70B，L=80、nkv=8、dh=128、BF16 每元素 2 字节，因此每 token KV cache 为 327,680 字节。单条 128k-token 序列会额外产生约 42 GB KV state；到 10^6 tokens 时约为 328 GB，相当于超过四张 H100 80GB 的总 HBM。算力利用侧，BF16 decode 的权重读取 intensity 约 1 FLOP/B，而 H100 ridge point 约 295 FLOP/B；GQA 即使 group 上，而是记录“已完成的 branch subgraph + 触发它的输入 + 它读过的外部依赖”。后续请求只有在输入精确匹配、且这些外部 reads 仍然新鲜时，才能消费该结果；一旦相关外部状态发生写入，就失效。这解决了 agent 工作流里 retrieval/tool 结果依赖外部环境、不能只靠 prompt exact match 复用的问题。\n\n第二层是 unresolved Three constraints must hold together: the reusable unit is an internal subgraph rather than a whole request; the key that authorizes reuse does not exist until the branch resolves, yet work should begin during that waiting window; and speculative execution must be priced against online serving load, otherwise a strategy that helps at low load can hurt under contention.","importance":"This is not a pretraining paper, but it is a meaningful serving paper for agent-native LLM systems. low-bit quantization of recurrent states in hybrid language models. Unlike ordinary activations or KV entries, errors in recurrent states persist and affect future readouts. Channels with slow decay retain quantization noise for many steps, while fast-decaying channels dissipate it quickly. Uniform range-based quantization therefore allocates precision without considering the future impact of the error.","importance":"The main value for pretraining and architecture work is the connection between hybrid-LM state dynamics and inference-time memory efficiency. Models such as Kimi Delta Attention, Gated DeltaNet, and Mamba-2 replace part of the attention cache with fixed-size recurrent states, shifting the systems bottleneck toward state storage, read/write bandwidth, and numerical precision. The paper provides a data-free, training-free, rotation-free allocation rule for recurrent-state quantization. It also makes a broader point: KV-cache quantization heuristics are not directly sufficient for recurrent architectures, because state errors have temporal dynamics. This can inform future choices of decay parameterization, state grouping, normalization, and quantization-friendly architecture design.","technical_approach":"The method assigns a distortion weight to each state channel using an observability Gramian. Under a local linear noise model, steady-state readout MSE can be approximated as sum_i Gamma_i sigma_i^2, where sigma_i^2 is the quantization noise variance for a row and Gamma_i measures how strongly that row’s error will be observed in future outputs. For diagonal decay without erasure, the paper derives Gamma_i = rho_i / (C expm1(2 s_i)), where s_i is the decay rate, rho_i is query-weighted energy, and C is the write-back interval. Slow decay therefore receives higher precision. These weights are combined with normalized state ranges inside output-normalization groups and plugged into a classical high-rate mixed-precision bit-allocation rule. Decay rates are quantized uniformly in log s, reflecting the sensitivity of long time constants to small relative changes in decay.","experiments":"The experiments evaluate three hybrid models and seven baselines. With per-token recurrent-state quantization, a 4-bit mean payload reduces excess negative log-likelihood by factors of 3.3 to 27.9 relative to the best baseline. At 6 bits, the NLL gap to the FP32-state baseline is below 0.005 nats. The paper includes ablations separating the contributions of variable bit widths, decay-aware weighting, range normalization, and logarithmic decay-rate quantization. It also reports an important caveat: deterministic rounding at C=1 can create correlated errors. In simulations using Kimi-like decays and rank-one writes, lag-one error correlations reach 0.23 for very slow channels, and three-to-five-bit readout error can range from 0.17x to 2.4x the independent-noise prediction. By six bits, discrepancies are typically within 20%. A fact retrieval task can often be solved by checking each document once, giving O(N) complexity. A contradiction-finding task may require comparing document or claim pairs, giving O(N^2) complexity. Similar issues appear for hybrid architectures that alternate linear and full attention, and for length generalization where a model is fine-tuned on shorter contexts than the intended test length. Repeated generations on the same benchmark item produce different binary outcomes, so the benchmark score is an estimate of expected performance. Uniformly repeating every item ignores the fact that item-level rollout variances differ: items with pass probability near 0.5 are noisy, while items near 0 or 1 need fewer samples.","importance":"This is an evaluation-method paper with practical relevance to pretraining and post-training loops. Checkpoint selection, RL iteration, agent workflow search, and automated research systems all depend on repeated evaluations. If rollout noise is large, small but real improvements can be missed, and noisy non-improvements can be selected. The contribution is a statistically better allocation of the same generation budget, yielding tighter estimates without changing the benchmark or model.","technical_approach":"The method, Speculative Evaluation, uses a Hierarchical Bayesian Neyman policy. For item i with pass probability p_i, the rollout variance is p_i(1-p_i). Classical Neyman allocation would assign more samples to higher-variance items if these variances were known. HBN handles the unknown-variance case with a two-stage design. It first runs a small uniform pilot over all tasks, fits a hierarchical Bayesian model to pool noisy success counts, and uses posterior expected sampling variances as allocation scores. It then performs exact positive-integer Neyman allocation for the remaining budget while keeping at least one fresh continuation sample per task. Pilot size and stage weight are chosen before evaluation, and a weighted estimator reuses the pilot without bias. HBN-async adds a systems component: it speculatively launches continuations from partial pilot feedback and retains only requests selected by the final allocation, reducing idle time at the pilot barrier.","experiments":"Across 107 benchmark–checkpoint profiles and average rollout budgets of 8–64 per task, HBN reduces estimator variance by 12.8%–33.6% on average relative to Uniform. This is a useful warning for long-horizon agent evaluation and retrieval-augmented systems: majority agreement and semantic deduplication can both be misleading when sources are correlated.","technical_approach":"CPB has two modes. A fixed gold rule promotes claims only when enough independent support remains after lineage collapse. CPB-Live runs agents against an actual shared store. 组织的结构化计划，覆盖场景、主体、动作、镜头语言、光照、音频/对白以及跨 shot 的叙事推进。它解决的是多因素耦合问题：动作变化会影响镜头运动，镜头运动又会影响节奏和转场，不能像普通 prompt rewrite 那样只做局部修饰。\n\n在 SFT 之后，作者引入 SC-GRPO。这里的重点不是 GRPO 本身，而是 reward 的设计。论文给了一个九维 semantic consistency reward，用来检查用户需求是否在整个计划中被完整保留，尤其关注四类错误：需求遗漏、语义篡改、实体/属性/动作绑定错误、时间顺序和跨镜头一致性冲突。相比只看最终文本质量或流畅度，这种 reward 更接近 structured fidelity。它的作用类似在长序列生成里加入一个全局 ","starred":true,"priority":"p1","reading_tier":"must_read","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-09-25T00:42:31Z","category_id":"post_train","cover_url":"/covers/2609_30652.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CL"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇论文解决的是 去掉外部 teacher，改用同一个初始 checkpoint 的拷贝作为 privileged teacher。teacher 的输入包含题目、ground-truth solution 和 student 当前生成的 prefix；student 只看到题目。这样 teacher 能在 gold-conditioned context 下提供更密集的 token-level The proposed mechanism is to train the model to predict its own confidence at intermediate reasoning states. Length, efficiency, and stopping are never direct training objectives.","importance":"The work is mainly a post-training study, but it is informative for the pretrain/post-train interface. At selected intermediate states, a fixed answer-elicitation prompt is appended, and the model greedily produces a trial answer. Confidence is defined as the geometric mean of the token probabilities assigned to that trial answer, i.e. a length-normalized likelihood under the model’s own distribution. It does not require gold labels or an external judge, and it is not treated as a calibrated probability of correctness. Fine-tuning examples then train the model to predict this confidence from the intermediate reasoning state. Reasoning tokens are masked out of the loss; only the confidence target is supervised. Those perturbations can act as behavioral projections of the update direction. This matters for two reasons. First, even a black-box teacher returning a single token can leak capability-relevant information. ATD uses M0 to select unrelated carrier prompts where two ordinary single-token candidates are nearly tied under the ancestor. Near such a decision boundary, a small post-training update can flip the preferred token. The teacher is queried only for one greedy next token, and the student trains on the resulting prompt-word pairs. No target-task data, teacher logits, long teacher generations, or teacher parameters are used. The paper motivates the design with a local linear approximation: the change in the logit difference between two candidate words is approximately the inner product between the post-training update and the carrier gradient direction. This separates two failure modes that are often conflated in practice. A run may fail not because the reward surface is full of traps, but because the policy update cannot diffuse across equal-reward deterministic codes, or because the signal-to-noise ratio is too poor without strong regularization and curriculum. The paper establishes three links: local reward maxima are continuously connected to deterministic policies without crossing a loss barrier; the entropy-regularized RLVR objective is lower-bounded by the free energy of the corresponding spin model; and trapped configurations under local spin dynamics approximately match RLVR fixed points. The task family is iterated group or quasigroup multiplication: the policy receives a sequence of elements, emits one intermediate token per step, and receives reward only when the final product is correct. The first model class is a bounded-window myopic tabular policy, chosen to expose properties of the RLVR objective before adding transformer parameterization effects.","experiments":"The theoretical result is that, for simple untied models with uncorrelated inputs, the reward landscape has no suboptimal local maxima. In contrast, exact local RLVR policy updates can fail in the same setting, because they do not move effectively across flat equal-reward regions. When weight tying or input correlations are introduced, the proof no longer applies, and local maxima appear in experiments. 的目标错配：若激活可分解为多个概念成分，重构损失对每个成分的奖励近似与其能量 E_j 成正比，因此高方差背景概念比低方差 forget 概念更容易被模型优先编码。这个分析不是严格现实假设下的定理，而是一个足够解释经验现象的 incentive model。\n\n基于这个问题，SCALPEL 不再只做重构，而是在 SAE 上加入针对 forget target 的对比学习。具体做法是：以 forget anchor 为中心，构造多个 paraphrase 和 rewrite 视图，把同一 anchor 的不同视图当正样本；负样本不从其他 forget 样本里取，而是从 retain 数据里取。这样做有两个目的。其一，不把 forget 集内部相关样本彼此推开，避免把目标概念自己打散。其二，把目标稳定出现的成分从共享语言模式、任务模式和背景语义里拉出来。训练完成后，SAE 给出一组固定的 sparse features，推理时对每个输入先经 encoder 判断哪些 forget features 被激活，再按强度减去对应 decoder 方向，形成输入相关的表示过滤。\n\n论文还有两个细节值得注意。第一，作者提出了 norm-aware feature selection，不只看 encoder activation，也看 decoder direction 的范数，因为真正的干预强度取决于“激活多少”和“沿哪个方向减去多少”。第二，理论部分给了三层论证：重构目标的 energy bias、加入 contrastive term 后更偏向 target-selective sparse representation、以及高分特征对背景扰动存在上界。这些理论更像方法合理性的支撑，而不是严格保证。","experiments":"实验在 TOFU 的 保真、特征选择性和重学/绕过风险。\n\n关键结果可以概括为四类。第一，在表示提取层面，SCALPEL 学到的特征比 reconstruction-only 方法更集中于 forget target，对 retain 数据的误伤更小。作者用背景激活投影、特征打分和可视化说明，标准 PCA/SAE 更容易吸收高能量背景结构，而 SCALPEL 提取的方向更贴近目标作者痕迹。第二，在 Given a set of tokens associated with the target attribute, it selects the corresponding columns of the unembedding matrix and treats them as a property-specific lexical subspace. These columns are the directions that the model decodes into the chosen vocabulary items at the logits. The method then scores attention heads by how well their residual contributions can be sparsely reconstructed from these property atoms, after accounting for the final normalization mismatch. During intervention, it does not add a difference-of-means vector to an entire layer. Instead, it selects a sparse set of aligned heads and projects the steering vector onto the corresponding lexical subspace before injecting it. This is stricter than head selection alone: head selection limits the location of the write, while subspace projection limits the directions that can be written.","experiments":"The paper evaluates the method on three models and three control settings: toxicity reduction, sentiment control, and sycophancy suppression. The reported pattern is that LocUS achieves the target behavioral shift while causing less damage to unrelated behavior than standard difference-of-means steering and localization-only variants. The important comparison is the control-versus-side-effect trade-off rather than a single task score. The key ablations examine head selection without subspace projection, different property token sets, and behavior under varying steering strengths.","reading_guide":"Skim the Introduction and Background to understand the failure mode of mean-difference steering: contrastive directions can contain off-target axes. For a matrix parameter of shape m by n, the friction state drops from O(mn) to O(m+n), while the full momentum buffer is retained. The discrete algorithm is derived from an ODE/Hamiltonian view and uses operator splitting: position drift, gradient kick, linear friction, and a coupled momentum-friction update. improve uniformly. The central issue is task structure. A team behaves differently when success depends on one member finding the right discrete answer than when success depends on averaging continuous estimates. Voting, pass@N, revision, and averaging have different statistical limits, so a single team-size scaling story is misleading.","importance":"The contribution is not a pretraining method, but it is useful for researchers working on test-time compute and model-output distributions. It shows that sampling more trajectories should not be interpreted as a direct gain in model capability. If errors are correlated, plurality voting converges to the model’s modal answer. If item-level bias dominates, averaging does little. These observations matter for designing self-consistency, debate data, verifiers, and evaluations of whether models provide genuinely diverse hypotheses.","technical_approach":"The authors use Steiner’s taxonomy of group tasks as the organizing frame. They focus on disjunctive tasks, such as QA and math problems where the team may succeed if one member is correct or if voting/verifier selection picks the right answer, and compensatory tasks, such as Fermi estimates where the team output is an average. They model independently sampled agents as conditionally independent given the item. Under this model, plurality voting converges to the model’s item-level modal answer, while averaging converges to the model’s item-level bias. This separates two mechanisms that are often conflated: the probability that the correct answer appears somewhere in the sample set, and the probability that aggregation selects it.","experiments":"The study evaluates 13 open-weight models with teams of up to 30 agents. On disjunctive tasks, pass@N increases with team size, with gains of roughly 5–20 percentage points. Plurality voting, however, is tightly bounded by the modal-answer limit; the conditional-independence model predicts large-team voting accuracy within about 0.5 points. Revision rounds improve accuracy, but using one peer gives nearly the same improvement as using 29 peers, suggesting that most of the benefit comes from a single perturbation rather than from scaling the team. On compensatory Fermi-estimation tasks, item-level bias explains about 87% of squared log-error, and averaging reduces error by only about 6%. Heterogeneous teams improve over their average member, but on disjunctive tasks they do not exceed the strongest member; for Fermi estimates, a five-model team of 7B–8B models can outperform its individual members.","reading_guide":"A skim is sufficient, about 25–35 minutes. trial 中，entity 和 obligation 来自不相交 token 池，模型必须在 query 后把正确 obligation token 排到最高 logit。chance level 是 obligation 池大小的倒数，文中为 0.040。k* 是 recall 低于“单绑定 K=1 表现”和 chance 中点时的最小 K，但作者明确指出阈值会制造不连续假象，所以进一步用 log K 上的 logistic fit 得到连续的 K50。论文还区分了容量轴 K 和干扰轴 D，并提出一个 interference identity：干扰可能只是降低 K=1 的单绑定可靠性，而未必改变负载相关的 recall 曲线形状。因此，比较模型时不能只看相对归一化后的曲线，也要声明绝对 recall 要求。","experiments":"实验包含两套测量。第一套是 30 个开放模型、10 个 family、最高到 12B 的 threshold sweep；剔除 K=1 接近 chance 的 Pythia-70M 后，k* 范围为 3 到 24，约 8 倍。三个模型在 k*=24 处触顶并被视为右删失：OLMo-1-7B、Qwen2.5-3B、OPT-6.7B。第二套是 12 个不超过 3B 模型的连续曲线重测，包括 OPT、Pythia、Qwen2.5、SmolLM2、OLMo-2 等 family。未删失拟合得到 K50 随参数量近似 N^0.820 增长，R² = 0.73。论文还报告 direct task training 相对零样本 scaling 外推可达到约 26 倍容量差距，但强调这是不同 estimand，且外推超出原任务负载域，不应直接解释为预训练能力同一曲线上的延伸。","reading_guide":"泛读建议用 20 到 30 分钟。重点看 Section 2 的任务定义、k* 和 K50 的差别；Section 3 的连续曲线拟合和右删失处理；Section 3.5 关于阈值迁移和模型排序变化的讨论；Section 6.1 的 interference identity。不要只记住 N^0.820 这个指数。更重要的是它如何避免把阈值现象误读为能力突变，以及如何区分单绑定可靠性、负载曲线、干扰鲁棒性和训练后可学习性。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper measures how many entity-value bindings a language model can keep track of in context before retrieval breaks down. The task is deliberately narrow: the model reads K assignments, passes through a distractor block, and must output the value bound to a queried entity. It isolates static binding recall rather than claiming to measure world-state tracking or multi-step state updates.","importance":"The useful contribution for pretraining research is a concrete capacity metric for in-context working memory, together with a careful separation between scale, recipe, interference, and task-specific learnability. On continuous recall curves for 12 models at or below 3B parameters, the measured half-recall load follows K50 = c N^0.820 with R² = 0.73. This is not a language-model-loss scaling law; it is an empirical law for zero-shot binding capacity. The broader sweep over 30 open models up to 12B shows large recipe-associated variation: for example, the Pythia ladder stays around k* = 3 to 6 from 410M to 12B, while Qwen2.5-3B reaches the measurement ceiling. The paper is appropriately cautious: in the continuous-curve subset, no clear recipe effect is detected after controlling for scale, partly because the number of modern models is limited.","technical_approach":"The task presents bindings of the form “entity: obligation”, where entities and one-token obligations are sampled from disjoint pools. After D distractor tokens, the model is queried with the entity and is counted correct if the correct obligation has the highest logit. Chance accuracy is 1 over the obligation pool, reported as 0.040. The discrete statistic k* is the smallest K where recall falls below the midpoint between the model’s own K=1 ceiling and chance. Because such thresholds can create artificial discontinuities, the paper also fits smooth recall-versus-log-K curves and reports K50, the continuous half-retention point. A separate interference analysis shows that distractors can reduce the single-binding ceiling without changing the load-dependent profile, which matters when comparing normalized curves across models.","experiments":"The threshold sweep covers 30 open models from ten families, ranging from GPT-2, OPT, BLOOM, Pythia, and Cerebras models to OLMo, Qwen2.5, Mistral, OLMoE, and DeepSeek-Coder variants. Pythia-70M is excluded because its K=1 accuracy is only 0.070 against 0.040 chance, making its threshold unreliable. After exclusion, k* ranges from 3 to 24, an 8x span. OLMo-1-7B, Qwen2.5-3B, and OPT-6.7B hit the k*=24 ceiling and are treated as right-censored. The continuous remeasurement covers 12 models at or below 3B and yields the N^0.820 fit. The paper also reports that direct task training can produce a factor-26 gain relative to an extrapolated zero-shot law, while emphasizing that this comparison mixes different estimands and extrapolates outside the original load range.","reading_guide":"A focused skim should take about 20–30 minutes. Read the task definition and metric construction in Section 2, then the continuous-curve analysis in Section 3. The most important methodological parts are the distinction between k* and K50, the handling of right-censoring, the threshold-transfer discussion in Section 3.5, and the interference identity in Section 6.1. The exponent is less important than the measurement discipline: the paper is mainly useful for thinking about how to evaluate in-context memory without confusing threshold artifacts, single-binding reliability, load sensitivity, and distractor robustness.","authors_note":""},"recommendation":{"zh":"只看容量定义、K50 拟合和 recipe 控制实验；12B 内结论外推风险大，但能给 ICL memory eval 一个干净变量。","en":"Read the capacity definition, K50 fit, and recipe-control analysis; extrapolation beyond 12B is weak, but the setup isolates a clean ICL memory variable."},"metadata":{"institutions":[],"authors":["Manas Venkata Sai Ravulapalli","Samrath Singh Chadha"],"notable_authors":[],"tags":["in-context-learning","binding-capacity","scaling-law","mechanistic-evaluation"],"links":{"arxiv":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30634","pdf":"https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.30634","github":null,"project":null,"source_url":null,"article":null}}}]}]}}]}]}]
